pull_requests.head: refactor/deep-cleanup-2026-07
pull_requests.body:
# Deep cleanup & modularization — dead code, security, architecture, bug fixes

**−12,516 net LOC · 20 commits · both suites green · 2 production bugs fixed**

Verified end-to-end: backend 248 tests, frontend tsc + 58 tests + Vite build, and
a local Firestore-emulator + Playwright E2E render (pixel-diffed).

## Why (IEC 62304 traceability)
Reduces review/maintenance surface on Class C modules, closes a credential leak,
and removes untraceable dead parallel implementations. No behaviour change except
the two bug fixes (each with a regression test).

## What changed

### Security
- Removed the hardcoded production admin password from **15** committed sites →
  `ADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD` env with fail-fast. **⚠️ Rotate the prod password — it
  is in git history.**
- `fix(auth)`: `register_user` logged a false "Failed to save user" ERROR on every
  successful registration (NameError on an undefined `username`). Fixed + verified
  E2E (201, zero false errors).

### Dead code (−13.7k LOC, verified unreachable)
- Backend: 3 unwired legacy services + an orphaned `segmentation_service_v2` provider.
- Frontend: an entire orphaned cache/perf/websocket/binary-protocol subsystem (~10.3k
  LOC incl. tests) that nothing imported.

### Architecture / modularity
- **segmentation.py god-router 2,263 → 3 focused modules** (crud 926 / regions / analysis),
  behaviour pinned by new black-box characterization tests (12).
- **Public SegmentationService API** — CRUD + analysis routes no longer reach into the
  private cache (0 reach-ins); `fix`: `GET /slice/{i}/mask` returned 500 on every call
  (`_array_to_base64` didn't exist) — now fixed with a regression test.
- **types/index.ts 1,365 → 7 domain modules** behind a barrel (51 consumers unchanged).
- **API clients consolidated** under `api/` (one convention).
- **ViewerApp** decomposed: 3 fragile heuristics → pure tested utils; `InstanceButton`
  and `SegmentationRow` extracted (the latter **pixel-diffed 0/921,600 px changed** on a
  real rendered study).

### Correctness
- `useSegmentationStore.reset()` shared-reference bug → `createInitialState()` factory.
- Removed write-only React state; fixed 3 stale UI tests (suite now fully green).

## Verification
- Backend: 248 pytest (unit + Class-C characterization).
- Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` clean, 58 vitest, `vite build` OK.
- **E2E**: local Firestore emulator + seeded study, headless Chromium render of ViewerApp;
  refactors confirmed by before/after pixel-diff.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
1. **Auth user-store durability (HIGH):** SecureUserStorage persists accounts to Cloud
   Run local disk (ephemeral/per-instance) while WebAuthn uses Firestore — accounts can be
   lost on redeploy/scale. Needs a storage design decision (Firestore? Secret Manager?).
2. Encapsulate the remaining 41 reach-ins in `segmentation_regions.py` (characterize the
   parcellation/lst-ai/msmask/zone-map branches first).
3. Route FHIR/DICOMweb reads through services (currently raw Firestore).

## Why

Preparing the app for examination by TUM/LMU faculty and Munich AI-market investors. Goal: **beautiful but maximally usable**, benchmarked against award-winning medical-imaging AI products (Viz.ai, Aidoc, Qure.ai). Direction chosen: **dual-register** — keep the clinical-dense rigor professors value in the *viewer*, elevate the *entry surfaces* (dashboard, patient detail, documents, PACS, profile) to a premium, confident register. Every change was verified against real rendered screens (local Firestore-emulator + backend + Playwright), not guessed.

## What changed

**1. One coherent shell (kills the "two apps" split)**
- Documents / PACS / Profile used bespoke headers (gradient clip-text titles, `Sparkles`, animated blur blobs, custom control rows) while Patients/Detail/Viewer used the v2.0 `AppHeader`. All three now render the shared MSTool-AI app bar with breadcrumbs on the `#030712` dark surface.
- `ThemeContext` defaults to **dark** (radiology/OHIF standard) unless the user saved an explicit choice — so `dark:`-variant pages render consistently.

**2. Cohort overview KPIs on the dashboard**
- Premium stat band (Patients / Active / MRI Studies / Documents) computed from **real cohort aggregates** — no fabricated AI numbers (honesty matters for an academic audience).

**3. Patient clinical-intelligence band**
- At-a-glance imaging summary derived entirely from the patient's own studies: Imaging Studies (+ modalities), **Monitoring Window** (first-to-latest scan span; "Baseline" for a single study — the core MS longitudinal-follow-up signal), Latest Scan, Imaging Data (image count + size). Fills the previously-empty column and surfaces MS domain context.

**4. Polish — two examiner-visible bugs killed**
- "41years" to "41 years" (missing space in the DOB/age line).
- Dates rendered in the **OS locale** leaked Spanish ("12 de jul de 2026") into an English UI. New shared formatDate util formats every date in the active i18n language; applied across 10 components. patients.clinical.* keys added in en/es/de.

## Verification
- tsc --noEmit: clean. npm run build: succeeds.
- Local E2E (Playwright, 1440x900): all 6 surfaces share one app bar, dark, **0 page errors**; dates render in English; clinical band renders from seeded study.

## IEC 62304 note
Frontend presentation-layer only. No Class C module touched. No requirement/risk-control logic changed.

pull_requests.title: QMS/safety: risk-control verification integrity — 5 CAPAs, 8 test-bound controls [Class C — REVIEW REQUIRED]
pull_requests.head: capa/rmf-verification-integrity
pull_requests.body:
## What this is

A QMS + safety-engineering body of work that turns the Risk Management File from a
document that **asserts** controls into one whose controls are **bound to tests
whose removal turns CI red**. It opened and worked five CAPAs (four Critical),
implemented eight new risk controls, and corrected the regulatory records that
were found to overstate what the code does.

**This is a REVIEW request, not a merge-ready change.** Per `CLAUDE.md`, Class C
modules must not merge without code review — and the whole point of CAPA-001 is
that single-party self-attestation is insufficient. It must not be treated as
closing any CAPA without independent Software Safety Officer verification
(CAPA-001 PA-3: the author of a control may not record its verification).

## ⚠️ Class C modules changed — require focused review

These are the highest-care files (per `CLAUDE.md`'s Class C list):

- `backend/app/services/brain_report_service.py` — RC-006 disclaimer (CA-1)
- `backend/app/utils/nifti_utils.py` — RC-023 orientation primitives (CA-4.1)
- `backend/app/services/lesion_analysis_service.py` — voxel spacing required (CA-5)
- `backend/app/services/ms_region_classifier.py` — voxel spacing required (CA-5)
- `backend/app/services/longitudinal_tracking_service.py`,
  `backend/app/services/segmentation_comparison_service.py` — voxel spacing (CA-5)

## The five CAPAs

| CAPA | Severity | What it found | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CAPA-001** | Critical | 4 controls recorded VERIFIED were absent; RCV summary said "Failed 0" | Re-verified all 22 (4 verified, 12 overstated/absent); RC-006/RC-017 implemented + test-bound; CI gate built |
| **CAPA-002** | Critical | Any authenticated user could read any patient's data (OWASP API1:2023) | Object-level authz enforced on **every** data surface (RC-026…029); SRS written; quarantine triage built. Enforcement complete; Safety-Officer verification pending |
| **CAPA-003** | Major | `tests/security/` had never executed (imported a module that never existed) | Added to CI as non-blocking + loud; repair tracked |
| **CAPA-004** | Critical | No L/R orientation handling and no patient identity in the viewport | Orientation primitives + viewport identity + Edge AI disclaimer + role authz (RC-023/025) |
| **CAPA-005** | Critical | Volumetry classifies atrophy against an **unsourced** normative table | Documented; blocked on the data source |

## Risk controls added, each with a measured negative control

Every control below is bound to a test whose removal was **verified to turn CI
red** — the negative-control counts are the measured evidence a reviewer can
re-run:

- **RC-006** report disclaimer — remove enforcement → 8 failed
- **RC-017** WebSocket auth — 2 vectors → 1 / 5 failed
- **RC-023** orientation "refuse to guess" — 2 vectors → 9 / 2 failed
- **RC-024** voxel spacing required — 2 vectors → 17 / 1 failed
- **RC-025** patient role authz — 3 vectors → 3 / 4 / 1 failed
- **RC-026** care-team object authz — 4 + 3 vectors
- **RC-027** imaging storage-ref parsing — 3 vectors → 1 / 2 / 2 failed
- **RC-028** study/document authz — 3 vectors → 1 / 2 / 1 failed
- **RC-029** segmentation authz — 2 vectors → 2 / 1 failed

The full binding is machine-checked in
`docs/iec62304/records/risk_verification/rc_test_manifest.json`, enforced by
`backend/tests/unit/test_risk_control_manifest.py`.

## Test status

Backend unit suite: **577 passing, 0 failing** locally. The 5 findings that were
transient came from missing dev deps in the local env, not the product; verified
with a baseline diff. Note the CI environment installs from `requirements*.txt`.

## What this does NOT do

- It does **not** close any CAPA. Effectiveness verification by the Safety Officer
  (QP-002 §4.6) is required, including an independent negative-control run.
- It does **not** make the device fit for clinical use. Four Critical CAPAs remain
  open; the RMF's residual-risk determinations for six hazards are **withdrawn**
  pending re-derivation.
- CAPA-002 residual work (documented, deferred with reasons): list result-level
  filtering, series/instance resolution efficiency (needs a Firestore-emulator CI
  test first), and Safety-Officer verification.

## Suggested review order

1. `docs/iec62304/records/capa/CAPA-001…005` — the findings and rationale.
2. The Class C module diffs above.
3. The authorization core: `backend/app/security/patient_access.py`,
   `storage_access.py`, `resource_access.py`, `patient_access_dependency.py`.
4. Re-run the negative controls from the manifest to confirm the evidence.

pull_requests.head: fix/route-module-imports
pull_requests.body:
## What happened

The backend deploy to Cloud Run failed its health check — `container failed to start and listen on PORT=8080`. Root cause: `NameError: name 'require_segmentation_access' is not defined` at `segmentation.py:150` during `app.main` startup. The RC-029 wiring lost the `from app.security.resource_access import ...` block.

## Why 601 tests + full CI missed it

**No test imported the route modules.** The RC-027/028/029 wiring tests read the route files as *text* (`.read_text()`) to assert a dependency string is present — they never `import` the module. `app.main` imports all 15 routes at startup, so the NameError only surfaced when the container started. A green suite proved the code parses and its units work; it did not prove the app can start.

## Fix

- Restore the full import block in `segmentation.py` (verified: `import app.main` succeeds; all 15 route modules import).
- Add `test_route_modules_import.py`: imports every route module **and** `app.main`, plus a drift guard keeping the list in sync with `app/main.py`. Negative control: reintroducing the dropped import fails the segmentation + app.main import tests (measured, restored).

Only `segmentation.py` was affected; the other 5 edited route modules import cleanly (verified). Backend suite: 601 passed.

pull_requests.title: feat(lesion): 18-connectivity + single documented min-volume floor (RC-030) [Class C]
pull_requests.head: feat/lesion-segmentation-soa
pull_requests.body:
## What & why

Grounded in a deep-research pass on the MS lesion-segmentation state of the art (22 claims confirmed, 3 refuted, primary sources). **Changes reported clinical numbers** (lesion count, DIS region-presence), so it is a risk-controlled change (RC-030, HAZ-005).

### The defect
Every lesion-counting site used `scipy.ndimage.label(binary)` with **no** `structure` = scipy's default **6-connectivity**. The two canonical MS challenges both define a discrete lesion as an **18-connected** component (ISBI-2015; MSSEG-2016). 6-conn over-splits edge-touching lesions → over-counts. Separately, `MIN_LESION_VOLUME_MM3 = 3.0` was duplicated and justified by a misleading '~3 voxels' comment; research showed the clinical '3 mm' is a **diameter** (~14 mm³), the LST-AI 3 mm³ claim was **refuted**, and the only genuine 3 mm³ basis is MSSEG-2016's evaluation gate.

### The fix
New `app/services/lesion_metrics.py` as the single source of truth: `label_lesions()` pins 18-connectivity; `MIN_LESION_VOLUME_MM3` re-anchored to MSSEG-2016 (explicitly **not** the 3 mm-diameter criterion). 7 lesion-counting sites rewired across 3 services; tissue/ventricle morphology helpers deliberately untouched. Longitudinal tracking now applies the same noise floor.

### Honest limits (recorded)
18-conn is the challenge-**evaluation** standard, not a clinical consensus. CC labelling can't separate **confluent** lesions, so count is inherently less reliable than volume/load (ρ ~0.92–0.97 vs ~0.83–0.94) — reporting must weight count accordingly.

### Evidence
`test_rc030_lesion_metrics.py` (11 tests) pins connectivity to **exactly 18** (edge-touching merges, corner-touching stays separate) and checks the end-to-end count. Negative control: revert to scipy default → 3 failed (measured). Backend suite: **612 passed, 0 regressions**.

⚠️ **Class C modules changed** (lesion_analysis_service, ms_region_classifier) — requires code review per CLAUDE.md. Full evidence in `docs/reviews/Lesion_Segmentation_Review_2026-07.md §7`.

pull_requests.head: test/rc031-orientation-characterization
pull_requests.body:
## What & why
Step 1 of the orientation fix (HAZ-006: mirrored overlay on square slices). The paint/render orientation path has a documented history of **5 failed fixes** — because on a 256×256 slice an in-plane-transposed overlay is dimensionally identical to an aligned one, so every dims-based test passes while the mirror ships. RC-023 (nifti_utils.py:45-53) requires "a test that loads a matched pair and asserts voxel correspondence" before any orientation change. This is that test. **Test-only — no Class C module modified.**

Proven on an asymmetric (Ni=5, Nj=8, Nk=3) volume, against real code:
- `generate_zone_map` is shape- and position-preserving (voxel-correspondence check) → **not** the transpose source.
- the GCS `np.transpose(...,(2,1,0))` save/load round-trip is self-inverse → **not** the source.
- the square-slice **blind spot** is locked in: the frontend `needsTranspose` heuristic returns False for both aligned and transposed overlays when i==j; on asymmetric data it can detect the transpose.

This isolates the divergence to the parcellation-branch serve path (which lacks the compensating transpose the MSMask branch correctly applies) and gives step 2 a fixture where the fix is verifiable.

6 passed. **Step 2** (compensating transpose on the parcellation serve path + voxel-correspondence assertion) is a Class C route change and ships separately once real parcellation order is observed.

pull_requests.title: fix(clinical-tools): make an all-zero sidecar mask visible, not silent (finding #7)
pull_requests.head: fix/clinical-tool-empty-mask-visibility
pull_requests.body:
## What & why
A clinical-tool sidecar (mindGlide/LST-AI/SynthSeg) can return HTTP 200 yet write an **all-zeros** mask (model didn't run, wrong contrast, off-grid resample). `_store_nifti_as_segmentation` stored it verbatim and marked the task COMPLETED — so "0 lesions" was **indistinguishable from a genuine negative**. A silent failure read as a clean scan.

**Control is visibility, not rejection.** An empty *lesion* mask is a valid clinical result (a healthy brain has zero lesion voxels), so failing it would be wrong. Instead:
- record `annotated_voxels` in the stored metadata → downstream can tell "found nothing" from "produced nothing";
- log a warning (validation_source + file_id) when a stored clinical-tool mask is all-zero → ops can investigate.

Not a Class C module. **Defense-in-depth** — these sidecars are behind feature flags (`*_ENABLED`); this hardens the path for when they're enabled.

## Tests (2, no Firestore/GCS)
- empty mask → stored, `annotated_voxels==0`, exactly one warning with context;
- populated mask → true count, no warning.

Ref: `docs/reviews/Lesion_Segmentation_Review_2026-07.md` finding #7.

pull_requests.title: feat(lesion): lesion-wise detection metrics (TPR/PPV/F1) alongside Dice
pull_requests.head: feat/lesion-wise-detection-metrics
pull_requests.body:
## What & why
Dice measures voxel **overlap** — it cannot tell whether the right **discrete lesions** were detected. Two segmentations with equal Dice can disagree sharply on detection. MS lesion segmentation is evaluated on **both** axes, and the detection axis is defined lesion-wise by the field's two reference challenges:
- **ISBI-2015** (Carass et al., NeuroImage 2017): a reference lesion is a TP when it overlaps the segmentation (LTPR / LFPR).
- **MSSEG-2016** (Commowick et al., Sci Rep 2018): 18-connectivity + overlap gate.

## Change
New `compute_lesion_detection_metrics(pred, ref, min_overlap_ratio=0.0)` → sensitivity (LTPR), precision (LPPV), `lesion_f1`, plus raw TP/FP/FN and component counts. It labels lesions with the **shared 18-connected convention (RC-030)**, so detection and the lesion **count** reported elsewhere agree by construction. `compare_two_masks` surfaces it under `lesion_detection` (B = reference, A = prediction). Backward-compatible (adds a response key).

Documented conventions: any-voxel overlap by default (ISBI); raise the ratio for MSSEG-style gating; vacuous rates = 1.0 (two empty masks agree, F1=1; empty-vs-populated, F1=0).

## Tests (10, + 25 existing comparison tests still green)
Perfect match; missed lesion → sensitivity only; spurious lesion → precision only; empty-mask conventions; **18-connectivity consistency with RC-030** (edge-touching = one lesion); overlap-gate rejects a grazing hit; wired into `compare_two_masks`.

Validation-metric foundation for **CAPA-005** (report lesion-wise F1 alongside Dice). Not a Class C module.

The clinician picks two saved segmentations of the current study — **A = prediction under test, B = reference** (e.g. AI or trainee vs expert) — and sees **both** quality axes:
- **Overlap:** Dice, Hausdorff, volume difference.
- **Detection:** lesion **F1**, sensitivity (LTPR), precision (LPPV), plus raw TP/FP/FN and per-mask lesion counts, labelled *18-conn, ISBI/MSSEG*.

Deliberately **not** added to LongitudinalCompare — that view is change-over-time (new/resolved/enlarged) with no ground-truth reference, so TPR/PPV/F1 would be semantically wrong there.

pull_requests.title: test(rc031): prove parcellation-overlay divergence from real code (step 1.5)
pull_requests.head: feat/rc031-parcellation-order-characterization
pull_requests.body:
## What & why
RC-031 step 1 ruled out the zone-map classifier and the GCS round-trip as the source of the mirrored parcellation overlay (HAZ-006), and proved **square slices hide any transpose**. It left the parcellation-branch axis order an *asserted* diagnosis — which gated the Class C serve-path fix (step 2) on "observing the real parcellation order".

This PR **closes that gate without real patient data or a Firestore emulator**, by driving the *actual* transform code on asymmetric synthetic data (`i != j != k` throughout, so any swap is a visible shape change).

## Code-proven facts
- **Painted masks** are `(depth,height,width) = (k,i,j)` and align with the displayed image (`segmentation_service.py:157`) — the display convention.
- The **GCS load transpose `(2,1,0)`** (`segmentation_service.py:905`) maps a parcellation NIfTI native `(i,j,k)` → **`(k,j,i)`**: the in-plane axes are swapped.
- **`generate_zone_map` is position-preserving**, so the parcellation-branch zone map inherits `(k,j,i)` and is served with **no** compensation → the mirror. The MSMask branch already compensates via `(2,0,1)` (`segmentation_regions.py:574`).
- The in-plane swap **`(0,2,1)`** carries `(k,j,i) → (k,i,j)` with **exact voxel correspondence**, proven on markers and through the real `generate_zone_map`.

## Scope (deliberate)
**Evidence only — does NOT touch the Class C serve path.** It establishes the exact compensating transpose and the voxel-correspondence assertion step 2 must carry, so the route change ships with proof instead of the fixed-transpose guesswork that failed 5× before.

## Open design question for step 2 (owner call)
The `(0,2,1)` compensation is correct for parcellations ingested from an external NIfTI (native `(i,j,k)`). If a parcellation could ever enter already in `(k,i,j)` (e.g. created via our own pipeline), a blind fixed transpose would *break* that case — so step 2 should either (a) apply `(0,2,1)` in the parcellation branch guarded by a provenance/shape check, or (b) reorient via the affine (`as_closest_canonical`) rather than a fixed permutation. This PR gives step 2 the test it must pass either way.

Risk control groundwork for HAZ-006. 5/5 pass. No Class C code modified.

pull_requests.title: feat(rc031): affine-based reorientation primitive (step 2, owner-chosen robust route)
pull_requests.head: feat/rc031-affine-reorient-primitive
pull_requests.body:
## What & why
Risk control for **HAZ-006** (mirrored / mis-oriented overlay). Step 1.5 (PR #12) proved the parcellation branch serves `(k,j,i)` while the display uses `(k,i,j)`, and that a **fixed** `(0,2,1)` swap corrects exactly that one orientation. You chose the **robust** route: align by the **affines**, not a fixed transpose — correct for *any* source orientation, which is precisely what the five prior fixed-transpose attempts lacked.

## Change (additive)
New `reorient_array_to_reference(data, source_affine, reference_affine)` in `nifti_utils.py`:
- permutes/flips a volume onto a reference voxel grid via nibabel `io_orientation`/`ornt_transform` (no resampling);
- **fails closed** on singular/non-finite affines — refusing to guess, per the RC-013 orientation-module philosophy.

## Tests (16) — physical correctness, not shape matching
The square-slice lesson is that equal dimensions prove nothing. Each orientation pair is generated with nibabel's own **inverse** transform, and the primitive is shown to:
- recover the reference grid **exactly** across 5 orientations (identity, in-plane swap, flips, full reverse);
- keep every marker's **world coordinate invariant** (the decisive physical check);
- **reproduce the `(0,2,1)`** swap for the RC-031 case *without hardcoding it*;
- be reversible; and **fail closed** on bad affines.

## Scope (deliberate)
Primitive + proof only. Wiring it into the zone-map parcellation branch (load parcellation + MRI NIfTIs with affines → reorient → `generate_zone_map`, guarded by a voxel-correspondence assertion) is the **serve-path** change and ships next — it benefits from validation against a real parcellation NIfTI or the Firestore emulator, so it is not bundled here.

Touches a Class C module (`nifti_utils.py`); additive function + tests, no existing behavior changed. Depends conceptually on #12.

## What deeper tracing found
A full trace of parcellation **affine plumbing** relocated the root cause and corrected my earlier "load path" hypothesis. The parcellation carries **no affine** by the time it is consumed — the clinical-tool ingest (`_store_nifti_as_segmentation`) loads the SynthSeg NIfTI, **discards `img.affine`**, and applies a blind fixed `np.transpose(mask_data,(2,1,0))` at `tool_runner_service.py:636`. That single line sets the parcellation's axis order for every downstream consumer.

- Ingest `(2,1,0)` → internal `(k, a1, a0)`.
- Display/painting convention — stated verbatim in the MSMask branch (`segmentation_regions.py:566-574`) and matched by painted masks (`segmentation_service.py:157`) — is `(2,0,1)` → `(k, a0, a1)`.

The in-plane axes are swapped ⇒ an ingested parcellation is the in-plane **transpose** of the display grid.

## Not just a cosmetic overlay bug
`classify_lesions_with_parcellation` (`ms_region_classifier.py:138`) requires equal shapes:
- **non-square** data → shapes differ → it **raises** (safe);
- **square 256×256** (the common MRI case) → shapes match → it **silently** compares each lesion voxel against the parcellation label at the *transposed* position → **mis-assigned MAGNIMS regions and DIS**. That silent path is the real hazard.

## Tests (5, all asymmetric so the swap is visible)
Ingest vs display transposes diverge by an in-plane swap; a square slice hides it; `(0,2,1)` reconciles ingest→display exactly; and the classifier shape-guard's two regimes are reproduced.

## Scope
**Evidence only — no behavior change.** The fix is affine-robust reorientation at ingest (`reorient_array_to_reference` to the MRI grid, then the `(2,0,1)` display transpose). Because it changes **clinical classification** and **stored-data semantics**, it ships separately with real-SynthSeg validation and a migration decision (see PR discussion). Builds on #12/#13. Risk control groundwork for HAZ-006.

## The fix
Fixes the root cause proven in #14. `_store_nifti_as_segmentation` applied a **blind `np.transpose(mask,(2,1,0))`** to **every** clinical-tool mask (SynthSeg, LST-AI, mindGlide), discarding the NIfTI affine → internal `(k,a1,a0)`, the in-plane **transpose** of the app's display convention `(2,0,1)` (painted masks `segmentation_service.py:157`, viewer `segmentation_regions.py:574`). Effect: mirrored parcellation overlay, and — because `classify_lesions_with_parcellation` only guards on equal **shape** — **silent MAGNIMS/DIS mis-classification on square 256×256 data**.

New `ToolRunnerService._orient_mask_to_display`:
1. reorients the mask onto the reference MRI's voxel grid **by affine** (`reorient_array_to_reference`, proven in #13 — correct for *any* source orientation, unlike the fixed transposes that failed five times);
2. applies the `(2,0,1)` display transpose.

Applied **uniformly** at all four ingest call sites (each referenced to the MRI it ran on: SynthSeg/mindGlide `input`, LST-AI `flair`), so every clinical-tool mask lands in **one** convention and `classify` stays mutually consistent — a SynthSeg-only fix would have *regressed* AI-lesion-vs-parcellation.

## Fails safe
If the reference MRI or a determinate affine is unavailable, it falls back to the legacy `(2,1,0)` — behaviour never regresses below today's baseline, and it never raises inside ingest.

## Tests (5) + regression
Geometry-preserving output lands in `(2,0,1)` (not legacy); a scrambled/canonicalised source is corrected before the display transpose; three fail-safe paths (no reference, missing file, singular affine) return legacy. **RC-031 + tool_runner suites: 41 passed, no regression.**

1. **Validate against one real SynthSeg/LST-AI run** — confirms the `(2,0,1)` display convention in vivo. Evidence is strong (#12/#13/#14) but a Class C change warrants one live check.
2. **Stored-data semantics** — existing masks were ingested with `(2,1,0)`; they must be **regenerated** (re-run the tool), not transformed. New ingests are correct from merge.

Class C impact (feeds `ms_region_classifier`). Depends on #14. Do not deploy before item 1.

## The original 131-day longitudinal-overlay bug
`_save_masks_to_gcs` stored masks with transpose `(2,1,0)` → on-disk `(a1,a0,k)`, the in-plane **transpose** of the MRI's native `(a0,a1,k)`, while attaching the MRI's affine. It round-tripped internally (load also used `(2,1,0)`), so the 2D editor looked fine and the bug hid — and on square 256×256 data the swap is dimensionally invisible (the RC-031 blind spot behind five prior failed attempts).

## Fix
Internal masks are `(k,a0,a1) = transpose(mri_native,(2,0,1))` — proven in #16 — so the inverse `(1,2,0)` restores the MRI's own array order. Save now uses `(1,2,0)` and **tags** the NIfTI header (`RC031-ORIENT-V2`); load reads the tag and uses `(2,0,1)` for tagged masks, `(2,1,0)` for legacy.

## Backward compatible — no bulk migration
Legacy (untagged) masks still load with `(2,1,0)` to the correct internal convention, so **existing data is unaffected**. New saves are MRI-native and align on direct serve. Re-saving a legacy mask upgrades it to v2 — gradual, optional migration. Applied to both the GCS and local-storage loaders; three pure helpers extracted and unit-tested.

## Tests (7) + regression
On-disk order is MRI-native; a v2-stored mask aligns voxel-for-voxel with the MRI grid while legacy does **not** (the mirror); v2 and legacy both round-trip to the correct internal convention; header marker detected across a real `.nii.gz` save/reload. **Full unit suite: 675 passed.**

One live visual check that a directly-served v2 overlay aligns (the reported symptom). **No data migration required** (unlike the clinical-tool fix #15).

Builds on #16 (display-convention proof). Core persistence path — please review with care.

pull_requests.title: fix(imaging): preserve HTTP status codes instead of remasking every error as 500
pull_requests.head: fix/imaging-status-code-masking
pull_requests.body:
## Context
Follow-up to the imaging P0 (#19). During that incident every original image surfaced as HTTP **500** — but the real cause was a **404** from the storage-ref gate. This PR removes the masking that hid it.

## The defect
All 8 imaging route handlers wrap their body in:
```python
except Exception as e:
    raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"...: {str(e)}")
```
That broad catch also swallows `HTTPException` and `AppException`, so:
- an auth / not-found **404** reached the client as a **500** (the confusing symptom during the outage), and
- `str(e)` leaked internal error text to the client.

It defeated all three registered global handlers (`AppException` / `HTTPException` / unhandled).

## Fix
Add `except (HTTPException, AppException): raise` before the broad catch in every handler. Intended status codes (400/401/403/404/409/…) now propagate to the global handlers; only genuinely unexpected errors become 500.

## Tests (4, unit)
CI runs `tests/unit/` only (the integration `conftest`/`async_client` is currently absent), so the guard is a unit test that calls the handler coroutine with the authz step monkeypatched: a raised `HTTPException(404)` propagates as **404** (not 500); `AppException` / `ImageProcessingException` propagate for the global handler; a generic `ValueError` is still contained as **500**. **Full unit suite: 687 passed.**

Not the P0 fix itself (that was the `.gz` allowlist, #19, already deployed + live-verified 200) — this is the diagnosability/correctness cleanup behind it.

pull_requests.title: fix(seg): selected-lesion bbox/centroid drawn transposed on non-transposed masks
pull_requests.head: fix/lesion-bbox-orientation
pull_requests.body:
## The bug
The selected-lesion overlay (yellow bounding box + red centroid crosshair) mapped backend coords to the display with an **unconditional** axis swap `y→X, x→Y` (commented "empirically confirmed").

But `analyze_lesions` computes bbox/centroid via `np.argwhere` on the **same `(D,H,W)` mask that is displayed** (`seg_data["masks_3d"]` from `get_loaded` — the same source as the binary `loadMask`). So `y` = height axis (i), `x` = width axis (j), and the correct display mapping is **`x→X, y→Y`**. The overlay *slice* is only transposed for display when the mask dims are swapped vs the image (the `needsTranspose` condition). **The bbox must follow that same transpose.**

## Effect
For every correctly-oriented mask — **all painted masks, all square 256×256 slices, and (post-RC-031) tool masks** — the box and crosshair were drawn **mirrored across the diagonal**, pointing at the wrong location. The old swap was correct only for the minority case (a non-square tool/zone mask that needs a display transpose). RC-031 (which corrects tool-mask orientation) widened the set of cases the unconditional swap gets wrong.

## Fix
Gate the bbox/centroid axis mapping on the **same `needsTranspose` flag** the mask render already uses: swap only when the mask is transposed for display, else map `x→X, y→Y`. Typecheck + build green.

## ⚠️ Visual QA before deploy
Canvas geometry is best confirmed by eye (the original "empirical" note shows the first author did too). Before deploying: select a lesion in an **asymmetric** study and confirm the yellow box lands on the lesion. Same posture as the RC-031 overlay gate. Not auto-deployed.

## Live-confirmed production outage
Minted a token and called the real endpoints on real segmentations in prod:
```
COMPARE         -> 500  "compare_two_masks() requires voxel_spacing..."
LESION-ANALYSIS -> 500  "...no image metadata. Voxel spacing is required..."
```
**The entire MAGNIMS analysis suite is dead in production.**

## Root cause
RC-024 made `voxel_spacing` mandatory, and these routes resolved it via `resolve_voxel_spacing(**segmentation** metadata)`. But `SegmentationMetadata` never carries `pixel_spacing`/`slice_thickness` (no `extra_fields`), so `resolve_voxel_spacing(seg_metadata)` **always raises**. The RC-024 unit test used a **mock** object with `extra_fields`, so it never exercised the real metadata — the suite shipped dead. `lesion-analysis`/`dis` are partly masked by their result cache; **`compare` (no cache) 500s on every call**, so the comparison panel (#11) was broken from the moment it shipped.

## Fix
New `_voxel_spacing_from_source_image(file_id, storage, ctx)` loads the segmentation's **source image** and returns `(dz,dy,dx) = (zk, za0, za1)` for the internal `(D,H,W)=(k,a0,a1)` mask order. Wired into all three routes (lesion-analysis + dis-assessment gain a `storage_service` dep; compare resolves from the first segmentation's source image or an instance NIfTI's own zooms, and now returns a clear **400** instead of a 500 when geometry is truly unavailable).

Pins that `resolve_voxel_spacing(real SegmentationMetadata)` raises (root cause), and that the source-image resolver returns correct `dz/dy/dx` from zooms with clean failures (missing file_id, unreadable image, non-3D). **Full unit suite: 697 passed.**

Changes clinical volume computation (voxel volume → MAGNIMS lesion-size thresholds → DIS). Restores dead functionality using the study's **real** geometry. pull_requests.title: fix(seg): stop silent data loss when a mask is missing from durable storage (P-2.1)
pull_requests.head: fix/segmentation-load-integrity
pull_requests.body:
## Data-integrity hazard (Class C)
A radiologist's segmentation could be **silently replaced with a blank mask** while the API reported "saved".

**Chain:** `_save_segmentation` wrote the Firestore doc **before** the GCS mask, so a GCS-upload failure left a doc pointing at a non-existent mask (the local fallback is ephemeral on Cloud Run). On the next load, `_load_segmentation` saw the doc, missed the GCS blob, and **fabricated `np.zeros(mask_shape)` returning success** — showing the clinician a blank mask in place of their work. `PUT /mask/binary` compounds it by reporting success from the in-memory voxel count regardless of whether the durable write landed.

## Two fixes
1. **Load fails loudly** — doc-exists + GCS-miss now tries the local fallback and, if unrecoverable, returns **False** (logged ERROR) instead of fabricating an all-zero mask. A blank mask is never presented as real data.
2. **Save writes GCS first**, then the Firestore pointer — a GCS failure leaves no doc claiming a non-existent mask, so the inconsistent state that fed the fabrication can't arise.

## Tests (3) + regression
doc-exists + GCS-miss + no-local → returns False and caches nothing; recovers via local when present; returns the real mask when GCS has it. **Full unit suite: 695 passed.**

Follow-up (separate): `PUT /mask/binary` should surface a failed durable save instead of reporting success from the in-memory count (P-4.3). Found in the segmentation audit (finding P-2.1).

pull_requests.title: fix(metrics): HD95 as surface-to-surface distance (MSSEG-2/Anima standard) — SOTA alignment
pull_requests.head: fix/hausdorff-surface-hd95
pull_requests.body:
## SOTA alignment + verified bug (audit A-4)
The MS field measures Hausdorff **surface-to-surface** (MSSEG-2 / Anima `animaSegPerfAnalyzer2`, ISBI-2015; MONAI/medpy). Our `compute_hausdorff` instead took distances over **every foreground voxel** (`dist_b[a]`, `dist_a[b]` with the full masks) despite the "surface distances" comment. Interior overlap (distance 0 wherever the masks agree) diluted the distribution and biased HD95 **optimistically low** vs the standard.

## Fix
Extract each mask's boundary (foreground minus its face-connected erosion; `border_value=0` so a mask reaching the volume edge is correctly treated as surface), then the symmetric 95th percentile of surface-A→nearest-surface-B and surface-B→nearest-surface-A distances (mm via the spacing-weighted EDT). This matches MONAI/medpy/Anima.

## Tests (7) — analytical ground truth, not the code
identical→0; single-voxel offset = exact distance; anisotropic spacing respected; a **contained** mask still reports the boundary gap (a full-volume metric's directed term is 0 there); offset solids report the surface shift; a solid vs its own **hollow shell** → ~0 (surfaces coincide) where a full-volume distance is large; empty conventions. These ground-truth tests **caught a `border_value` slip in my first cut** — the value of testing against known geometry, not against the implementation. **Full unit suite: 707 passed.**

## Class C
Changes the reported Hausdorff (a validation/QC metric). HD95 values will rise to the standard surface figure. Merging auto-deploys.

Grounded in the state-of-the-art review (MSSEG-2/Anima metric conventions).

pull_requests.title: feat(volumetry): BPF + annualized PBVC — MS atrophy to SOTA (SIENAX/icobrain/NeuroQuant)
pull_requests.head: feat/volumetry-bpf-pbvc
pull_requests.body:
## What & why

Brain volumetry reported raw structure volumes and a **raw % change over an arbitrary interval**. That is below the MS-atrophy state of the art. Commercial (icobrain ms, NeuroQuant/LesionQuant, cNeuro) and academic (SIENAX/SIENA) tooling report:

1. **Head-size-normalized brain volume** — Brain Parenchymal Fraction (BPF = brain parenchyma / intracranial volume). Raw brain volume is confounded by head size and not comparable across patients/scanners.
2. **Annualized atrophy rate (PBVC, %/year)** — the pathological cutoff is ~**-0.4%/yr** vs ~0.1-0.3%/yr in normal aging. A raw % over an unknown interval cannot make that distinction (-0.6% is normal over 3yr, pathological over 6mo).

This PR closes both gaps.

## Changes

**Backend**
- `compute_volumes` → `brain_parenchymal_fraction` (from voxel counts; excludes ventricles/CSF; `None` when ICV empty).
- `compare_timepoints` → annualizes change from timepoint ISO dates; adds whole-brain **PBVC** and **BPF** change rows with `is_pathological_atrophy` (flagged against -0.4%/yr); exposes `interval_years`.
- Degrades gracefully: missing/unparseable/equal dates → `annualized_change_percent = null`, raw change still reported. Sort key hardened against present-but-`None` dates.

**Frontend**
- `brain_parenchymal_fraction` on `VolumetryResult` + a dedicated **BPF card** in `BrainVolumetryPanel`.
- `VolumetryChange` typed for the annualized/PBVC/pathological fields.

## Compatibility
Fully backward compatible — whole-brain rows appear only when timepoint dicts carry the optional `total_brain_volume_ml` / `brain_parenchymal_fraction` keys; the request schema is unchanged.

## Testing

pull_requests.head: fix/paint-readonly-mask
pull_requests.body:
## Bug (audit P-1.1)

`PUT /{id}/mask/binary` builds the cached mask with `np.frombuffer(mask_bytes, ...)`, which returns a **read-only** array backed by the immutable request bytes. A subsequent `/{id}/paint` stroke edits that array **in place** (`_apply_circular_brush` → `mask[y0:y1, x0:x1] = value`) and raised:

```
ValueError: assignment destination is read-only  -> HTTP 500
```

So painting after a full-mask upload was broken.

## Fix
- **Ingestion** (`routes/segmentation.py`): `.copy()` the `frombuffer` array → writable, C-contiguous cached mask.
- **Defense-in-depth** (`services/segmentation_service.py`): `apply_paint_stroke` promotes any non-writable cached mask to writable **once** before painting, covering other immutable-buffer ingestion paths (mmap load, cache deserialization). Uses `.copy()` deliberately — `np.ascontiguousarray` is a no-op on an already-contiguous read-only array and would leave it read-only.

## Tests
New `test_paint_readonly_mask.py`: drives `apply_paint_stroke` on a **real read-only `frombuffer` mask** (read-only precondition asserted) — paint succeeds, the cached array becomes writable, edits accumulate across strokes. Written as `async def` (repo `asyncio_mode = auto`); `asyncio.run()` would close the shared loop and pollute later async tests.

Full backend unit suite green (**732 passed**).

## IEC 62304 (Class C)
Touches `segmentation_service.py`. Restores a broken editing path (data-entry correctness); no change to mask semantics or orientation. Low risk, additive guard.

pull_requests.title: harden(segmentation): pin label-mask verbatim invariant vs inherited scl_slope (P-4.1)
pull_requests.head: harden/label-nifti-no-scaling
pull_requests.body:
## Context (audit P-4.1)

`_save_masks_to_gcs` reuses the **source MRI header** so the segmentation NIfTI is voxel-for-voxel aligned with the MRI (ITK-SNAP). That header can carry a non-unit `scl_slope`/`scl_inter`. Label masks are **categorical** — any intensity scaling on write/read would corrupt class IDs.

## Honest finding: NOT an active bug

Verified empirically across `slope ∈ {0.5, 2.0, 10.0}` (+ non-zero inter), labels up to 200: `set_data_dtype(uint8)` makes nibabel **recompute** scaling for the integer output and reset `scl_slope/inter`, so labels survive intact. The audit's "labels can be scaled/truncated" was theoretical. No production data was affected.

## What this PR does (defense-in-depth, Class C)

The invariant shouldn't rest on implicit nibabel behavior:
- `header.set_slope_inter(1.0, 0.0)` before writing the label NIfTI — makes "labels are verbatim" **explicit**.
- `test_label_nifti_no_scaling.py` drives the **real** `_save_masks_to_gcs` through a fake GCS bucket (source header slope 2.0/0.5/10.0), asserting round-tripped labels (incl. a large label 200) are intact and the persisted header applies no scaling. Guards against a future nibabel/code change silently reintroducing scaling.

No behavior change to persisted data (already correct); this pins and documents the invariant. Full unit suite green (**735**).

pull_requests.title: fix(longitudinal): A-3 — refuse cross-grid compare instead of silent square-blind transpose
pull_requests.head: fix/longitudinal-grid-guard
pull_requests.body:
## Bug (audit A-3, RC-031 class)

`/longitudinal/compare` loads both timepoints in the **same canonical internal order** (RC-031 for segmentations; the `(2,0,1)` transpose for instances — A-1). When the two shapes differed, the route transposed TP2 to whatever axis permutation made the **dimension sizes** line up:

```python
# old: greedy size-matching permutation
for t in target:
    for i, s in enumerate(source):
        if s == t and not used[i]: perm.append(i); ...
mask_tp2 = np.transpose(mask_tp2, perm)
```

Unsafe because:
- matching dimension **sizes ≠ matching anatomical axes**, and
- when two dims are equal (**square in-plane**, e.g. 256×256) the permutation is **ambiguous** and picked arbitrarily.

→ a plausible-but-wrong longitudinal result (new / resolved / enlarged lesion counts) with **no error surfaced** — a Class C hazard.

## Fix

Both masks are already canonically oriented, so **equal shapes ⇒ same voxel grid** and the comparison is valid; a genuine mismatch between independent acquisitions needs **registration/resampling**, not an axis permutation. Replaced the greedy realignment with `_require_comparable_grid()`, which **fails loud (HTTP 400)** with a specific message distinguishing:
- *same dims, different axis order* → needs registration (refused to avoid silent mis-alignment), vs
- *different voxel grids* → must be resampled to a common grid.

## Tests
`test_longitudinal_grid_guard.py`: identical shapes pass; the **square-ambiguous swap**, an all-distinct permutation, and a true grid mismatch are each rejected with the right hint. Full unit suite green (**740**).

## Compatibility
The only flows this changes are exactly the shape-mismatch cases that were previously silently transposed — post-RC-031 those are the mis-aligned ones. An honest 400 (surfaced in the LongitudinalCompare UI) replaces a wrong result.

pull_requests.title: fix(segmentation): P-4.3 — report save durability honestly (no false success on ephemeral fallback)
pull_requests.head: fix/persist-durability-honest
pull_requests.body:
## Bug (audit P-4.3)

`_save_segmentation` falls back to an **ephemeral local** write when GCS/Firestore fails, but returned nothing. So `PUT /{id}/mask/binary` reported an unqualified `success: True` even when the clinician's edit was saved **only to local storage** — lost on Cloud Run instance restart, invisible to other instances. The frontend then cleared its dirty flag and discarded the local backup: **silent data loss**.

## Fix

**Backend**
- `_save_segmentation` / `persist` return the **durability tier**: `"gcs"` (durable), `"local"` (ephemeral fallback only), or `None` (nothing to save). Still raises only if **both** tiers fail.
- `PUT /mask/binary` adds `durable` + `storage` to the response; when not durable it returns an honest warning message and logs a warning. `success` stays `true` (request accepted) but `durable: false` tells the client the truth.

**Frontend** (`useSegmentationMask.save`)
- Checks `durable`: a non-durable save **no longer clears `isDirty`** (keeps the local edit as backup) and surfaces the warning; returns `false`. `durable` absent (older backend) ⇒ treated as durable (backward compatible).

## Tests
`test_persist_durability.py`: `persist` → `"gcs"` on success, `"local"` when GCS raises (local fallback invoked), `None` when absent, and re-raises when both tiers fail. Full backend unit suite green (**744**). Frontend `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## IEC 62304 (Class C)
Touches `segmentation_service.py`. Converts a silent-data-loss path into an honest, recoverable one (keeps local backup + warns). No change to the durable-save happy path.

pull_requests.title: feat(dis): McDonald 2024 — 5 topographies, DIT-waiver signal & CVS/PRL/CSF specificity
pull_requests.head: feat/dis-mcdonald-2024-five-topographies
pull_requests.body:
## Vanguard: 2024 McDonald criteria (verified before building)

Confirmed against the **2024 revision of the McDonald criteria** (Montalban et al., *Lancet Neurology* 2025) and the 2025 AJR/Continuum radiologist guidance. Key 2024 advances our DIS tool didn't model:
- **Optic nerve = 5th topography** (was 4).
- With lesions in **≥4 of 5 topographies, dissemination in time may be waived**.
- **Central vein sign, paramagnetic rim lesions, and CSF-specific findings** (OCB / elevated κ-FLC) add specificity.

These are **achievable now** — pure criteria logic, no SWI/phase data or ML required.

## What changed

**Backend** (`lesion_analysis_service.compute_dis_criteria`)
- Keyword-only optional evidence: `spinal_cord_involved`, `optic_nerve_involved`, `cvs_positive`, `prl_present`, `csf_specific`.
- New output: `total_topographies_involved` (across all 5), `dis_met_full`, `dit_waiver_supported` (≥4/5), `supportive_specificity_markers`, `specificity_marker_present`, `external_evidence_provided`, and a `decision_support_note`. **All prior fields preserved** — a brain-only call is byte-for-byte compatible.
- `GET /dis-assessment` accepts the evidence as optional query params; the **cache is only used for the unparameterized brain-only assessment**, so a parameterized result never pollutes or is served from it.

**Frontend**
- `DISAssessment` / `DISExternalEvidence` types; `getDISAssessment(evidence?)`.
- `LesionDashboard`: 5-topography count, a **DIT-waiver banner**, specificity note, and checkboxes for external evidence that **re-query live**.

## Framing (Class C / CMSC)
Everything is presented as **radiological decision support, never a diagnosis** — the tool never asserts "McDonald criteria met/not met"; every surface repeats "requires clinical correlation."

## Tests
`test_dis_mcdonald_2024.py` (9): optic-nerve-as-5th, DIT-waiver at ≥4, cap at 5, False-vs-None evidence semantics, specificity markers, decision-support framing, brain-only backward compatibility. Full backend unit suite green (**753**). Frontend `tsc` clean.

## Sources
- [2024 revisions of the McDonald criteria — Lancet Neurology](https://www.thelancet.com/article/S1474-4422(25)00270-4/abstract)
- [The 2024 Update to the McDonald Criteria: A Guide for Radiologists — AJR](https://www.ajronline.org/doi/10.2214/AJR.25.33997)

Builds a manifest of the expert masks we already hold (incl. the ISBI-2015 2-rater set) to feed the Phase-1 benchmark engine and the Phase-3 automated-segmenter benchmark.

pull_requests.title: feat(segmentation): CALM-MS core — conformal lesion-FDR control + benchmark aggregation
pull_requests.head: feat/calm-ms-conformal-core
pull_requests.body:
## The computational heart of CALM-MS

The first two publishable contributions of the [CALM-MS master plan](../), as verified, model-agnostic code. Pure NumPy, no I/O, no GPU.

### C1 — Conformal lesion-level FDR control (`conformal_lesion_fdr.py`)
The novel contribution. Given per-lesion confidence scores from **any** base segmenter (LST-AI, nnU-Net, a foundation model, the legacy AI):
- **conformal p-values** (Jin & Candès 2023): `p = (1 + #{cᵢ ≥ s}) / (n+1)` — super-uniform under the null by exchangeability;
- **Benjamini-Hochberg** at level α selects a subset with **FDR ≤ α**, distribution-free.

This turns the over-segmentation we **measured on our own data** (lesion precision ≈ 0.22) into a **guaranteed, clinician-set operating point** — the product's false-positive dial *and* the paper's guarantee. Conformal risk control has never been applied to MS lesion segmentation.

**The test proves the theorem, it doesn't assert it:** a Monte-Carlo test verifies realized FDR ≤ α across simulated cohorts for α ∈ {0.05, 0.10, 0.20}, plus dial-monotonicity and high-power checks.

### C4 — Benchmark aggregation (`segmentation_benchmark.py`)
Multi-case reporting the field's "rethinking evaluation" work asks for: mean/median/std/IQR, **percentile bootstrap 95% CIs**, and **micro** (pooled TP/FP/FN) vs **macro** (per-case F1) lesion-detection.

### Metrics fill-in
`compute_jaccard` (IoU) and `compute_avd` (normalized absolute volume difference) added to the comparison service.

## Tests
26 new unit tests (incl. the FDR-guarantee Monte Carlo). Full backend unit suite green (**807**).

## Scope
Library core only — model-agnostic, no serving/route wiring yet. Next: wire the dial into the app (precision slider + per-lesion confidence overlay) and run the FDR-coverage experiment on real cases.

pull_requests.title: feat(segmentation): CALM-MS inference layer — probability map → risk-controlled mask
pull_requests.head: feat/calm-ms-inference-layer
pull_requests.body:
## The bridge: base segmenter → conformal guarantee

Builds on the CALM-MS core (#36). Turns any probabilistic segmenter's output into a **risk-controlled** lesion mask, and provides the data pipeline for the paper's FDR-coverage experiment.

- **`extract_lesion_candidates`** — soft probability map → 18-connected components → per-lesion confidence (mean or peak posterior), volume-filtered (3 mm³).
- **`build_calibration_nulls`** — match candidates to expert GT, collect the **false**-candidate scores = the conformal null distribution.
- **`select_lesions_conformal`** — end to end: selects the candidate subset with expected **lesion-level FDR ≤ α**, paints the final mask, and attaches a **calibrated per-lesion confidence** (`1 − conformal p-value`). `α` is exactly the product's "false-positive tolerance" slider.

## The proof
The headline test runs the **full pipeline on synthetic probability volumes** and verifies realized lesion-FDR ≤ α across 120-cohort Monte Carlo (α = 0.10, 0.20) — the mask-level guarantee, not just abstract scores. Plus dial-monotonicity, TP/FP labelling, calibration, volume-filter, and score-pooling tests.

**10 new tests. Full backend unit suite green (817).** Pure NumPy/SciPy, model-agnostic.

## Where this sits
Library layer complete: `prob_map → guaranteed lesion mask + per-lesion confidence`. Next: (a) wire it behind a route + the UI precision dial / confidence overlay, and (b) feed it real probabilities from LST-AI (deploy sidecar) or our own backbone to run the FDR-coverage experiment on the 19 expert cases.

## The plot that is the paper

Completes the CALM-MS pipeline (core #36 + inference #37). Given a cohort of **(probability map, expert mask)** pairs, `run_loo_fdr_experiment` runs **leave-one-case-out**: calibrate the conformal null on every other case, select on the held-out case, and report — per target α — **realized lesion-level FDR (bootstrap 95% CI)** and **lesion sensitivity**, against the **uncontrolled baseline** (keep everything at threshold) where today's over-segmentation lives.

- `backend/app/services/conformal_experiment.py` — pure engine (LOO, per-case candidate prep, FDR + lesion sensitivity, baseline).
- `scripts/run_conformal_experiment.py` — loads NIfTI `(prob, gt)` pairs (manifest CSV or `{case}_prob/_gt` dir convention) and prints the FDR-coverage table + JSON.

## Tests
Realized FDR ≤ target across held-out synthetic cases; baseline FDR high (>0.3); target→realized→sensitivity tradeoff monotone. **3 new tests, full suite green (820).**

## The one remaining input: real probabilities
Everything is ready to run **for real** the moment we have per-voxel probability maps. Fastest path — run **LST-AI locally** (`pip install`, the same 3×U-Net ensemble already referenced in the app, emits a lesion probability) on the cohort's **T1w+FLAIR**; the `Expert Rater` masks are the ground truth. pull_requests.title: fix(classc): region classification shows evidence, never a fabricated per-lesion confidence (REQ-SAFE-010, HAZ-005)
pull_requests.head: fix/region-confidence-honesty-haz005
pull_requests.body:
## What changed and why

**Implements REQ-SAFE-010 (amended 2026-09-28). Risk control RC-010 (amended) for HAZ-005.** Closes audit finding #8 ("fabricated confidence"), which had never been located.

The MAGNIMS region-classification table showed a per-lesion "confidence %" with green/yellow/red badges and an "Avg confidence". No classification path has a calibrated per-lesion probability — region assignment is a deterministic MAGNIMS rule — yet:

- the **parcellation** path (used in `auto` whenever any sibling segmentation contains ≥3 FreeSurfer-range label values) returned a distance linearly mapped onto **0.70–0.95** (DWM 0.60–0.90);
- the **MSMask** path returned a fixed **0.50** for lesions outside every zone, and otherwise an in-zone fraction whose denominator excluded non-zone voxels (a sliver-contact lesion could show 100 %);
- the **MCP clinical server** forwarded these numbers to the AI assistant, which could repeat "92 % confidence" in a report.

The 2026-07-18 RMF row recorded the confidence as "deliberately absent" because the geometric path emits `None`; it missed the other two paths.

### Backend (Class C module `ms_region_classifier.py`)
- `confidence = None` on **every** path, with a `confidence_note`.
- Evidence under honest names: parcellation → `distances_mm` (**`None` when a landmark is absent** — previously `inf`, which the route sanitiser turned into `0.0`, i.e. "touching"); MSMask → `region_overlap_fraction` (share of **all** lesion voxels in the assigned zone), `zone_coverage_fraction`, `atlas_coverage` (false ⇒ Deep White Matter assigned **by default**, with an explicit note — a possible DIS false negative).
- **Region assignment is unchanged** (MAGNIMS contact rule IT > PV > JC > DWM; distance thresholds untouched; verified by diff and boundary tests).
- `region_evidence.strip_region_confidence` nulls confidences in classifications persisted before this change before the MCP server forwards them; MCP tool docstring no longer promises a confidence.

### Frontend
- `LesionDashboard.tsx`: no certainty colouring, no average confidence; neutral **"Lesion % in zone"** column rendered as e.g. "8% in PV"; lesions in no white-matter zone get an **amber data-quality warning** "No WM zone — DWM by default" with a tooltip asking to verify the location before DIS; summary states that regions follow a deterministic rule. i18n en/es/de.
- `utils/regionEvidence.ts` ignores any `confidence` even if a stale backend sends one.

### Documents
SRS v1.1 (REQ-SAFE-010 amended, covers emission and display), RMF v1.2 (original RC-010 row retained and marked SUPERSEDED; amended row with executed negative controls; HAZ-005 residual stays **UNDETERMINED** — this control is information-for-safety only and region-assignment accuracy is unmeasured), `rc_test_manifest.json` (RC-010 → implemented, correct hazard HAZ-005, tests, negative control), traceability matrix, DDS (DD-CLS-001), V&V plan, master compliance document, IFU, UEF, CER, AI-Act file, README, CAPA-001 addendum and RCV-SUMMARY erratum.

## Verification
- `backend/tests/unit/test_region_confidence_haz005.py` — 7 `test_rc010_*`.
- `frontend/src/components/LesionDashboard.haz005.test.ts` — 7 `rc010` cases.
- **Negative controls executed** (mutate → run → restore): numeric confidence restored on parcellation → 2 failed; 0.50 fallback → 1 failed; old denominator → 1 failed; `round(inf)` distances → 1 failed; UI confidence cell → 1 failed; `regionEvidence` returning confidence → 1 failed. Restored: all green.
- Risk-control manifest gate (`test_risk_control_manifest.py`): 166 passed.
- Full backend unit suite and full frontend suite (110 tests) green; `tsc --noEmit` clean; production build OK.

## Review
Adversarially reviewed by 4 independent lenses (clinical safety, API consumers, test adequacy, IEC 62304 traceability) + a verdict pass: the first version was **not merge-ready** (14 required fixes, including the misleading overlap denominator and `inf → 0.0` distances); every required fix is applied here. **A human code review of the Class C module is still required before merge (CLAUDE.md).**

## Known, tracked, out of scope
- The parcellation-candidate heuristic (`≥3 FreeSurfer-range labels`) can select a sibling segmentation that is not a parcellation — pre-existing; recommend a CAPA.
- The LST-AI path's `total_classified` counts voxels, not lesions — pre-existing.
- i18n JSON files contain duplicate keys (JSON.parse keeps the last) — pre-existing.
- HAZ-005 needs a measured region-assignment accuracy (expert region labels) before its residual can be accepted.

pull_requests.title: fix(classc): MAGNIMS path preconditions, region-route outage, labelling (CAPA-006, RC-032, REQ-SAFE-021, HAZ-005)
pull_requests.head: docs/labelling-magnims-method-capa006
pull_requests.body:
## MAGNIMS region classification: path preconditions enforced, region-route outage fixed, authorization, labelling corrected (CAPA-006, RC-032)

Implements REQ-SAFE-021 (new) and REQ-FUNC-053 (corrected) as risk control RC-032 for HAZ-005 (a wrong MAGNIMS region leads to a wrong DIS). Records errata to RC-024 / CAPA-001 CA-5 and to RC-029 (HAZ-010). Opens CAPA-006.

> ⚠️ **Modifies a Class C module (`ms_region_classifier.py`) and the region routes.** Per CLAUDE.md this must not merge without human code review.

### Why
The IFU, AIA and GSPR were **issued on 2026-04-12 stating 3 / 4 / 3 mm** MAGNIMS thresholds; the CER stated 3 / 4 mm. The code had applied 1.5 mm ("direct contact") since 2026-02-28. Investigating that mismatch, and the five adversarial reviews that followed, uncovered the following:

1. **Outage.** `classify-regions` and `generate-zone-map` have returned **HTTP 500 on every call** since 2026-07-18. This is a CAPA-001 CA-5 regression: spacing was resolved from `SegmentationMetadata`, and there were undefined names.
2. **Atlas used off-MNI.** The **MNI152 MSMask atlas was applied to non-MNI images** without registration. Moving the anatomy by up to 3° / 3 % / 5 mm changed the region of **27.5 %** of expert lesions and brain DIS in 4/30 scans. A weak copy of the gate has also been live in the **longitudinal compare** route since 2026-08-22.
3. **Wrong axis order.** Atlas zone maps were combined in the wrong axis order: rotated on cubic grids, and transposed after a GCS reload because of a raw overwrite with no RC-031 marker.
4. **Wrong parcellation.** A **zone map, an instance-labelled mask or another image's segmentation was accepted as a FreeSurfer parcellation**. For a zone map, DWM was read as the ventricle, so DWM lesions came out Periventricular.
5. **Geometric fallback.** It dropped the brain outline on non-cubic images, so JC was under-counted, which can give a false-negative DIS. It also ignored orientation.
6. **No authorization.** Both region routes lacked **object-level authorization**. RC-029 was wired only in `segmentation.py`, before the C3 split.
7. **Faults reported as refusals.** Faults were reported as refusals or degraded silently, and the zone-map replacement was not atomic.

### What changed
**Code** (`ms_region_classifier.py`, `segmentation_regions.py`, `segmentation_analysis.py`, MCP docstring):
- **`looks_mni`** requires all of:
  - isotropic voxels;
  - axes aligned and not permuted;
  - field of view within 25 % of the MNI box, **per axis**;
  - grid centre within 10 mm of the MNI template centre;
  - a header transform.

  It is the single gate, shared with the longitudinal route.

Implements REQ-SEC-001 (RC-029, completed) for HAZ-010. Opens CAPA-007.

### Why
The C3 refactor (`5ebe5f6`, 2026-07-10) moved routes out of `segmentation.py` before RC-029 was wired there. The RC-029 verification read that one file, so **eight live analysis routes checked authentication only**:

- lesion-analysis
- dis-assessment
- lesion-annotations (a write)
- export/dicom-seg
- compare
- agreement-map
- longitudinal/compare
- longitudinal/sel

In addition, `compare` used a **client-supplied `gcs_path` as the storage key**, so any stored object was readable. This is the RC-027 class of defect.

### What changed
- **Path routes**: `lesion-analysis`, `dis-assessment`, `lesion-annotations` and `export/dicom-seg` now depend on `require_segmentation_access` (404 when the caller may not access the patient).
- **Body routes**: `compare`, `agreement-map`, `longitudinal/compare` and `longitudinal/sel` call the new `resource_access.authorize_mask_specs()`. Every segmentation or instance the body references is authorized (404); an unknown type returns 400.
- **Storage path**: `compare` ignores any client `gcs_path` and uses only the authorized instance's own object path.

### Verification

  - every other `/segmentation` route must be classified and must call its scope authorization;
  - a caller without access gets 404 on all eight routes;
  - a client `gcs_path` is ignored.
- **Updated tests**: two existing route tests now pass authorization through explicitly. One of them relied on the client `gcs_path`.

pull_requests.body:
## What changed and why

**CAPA-008 (Critical)** — record: `docs/iec62304/records/capa/CAPA-008_AI_Assistant_Layer_And_Clinical_Rule_Fidelity.md`

The MCP assistant layer (off by default, never deployed) was outside risk management:
- it could **write clinical records** (CVS/PRL readings that feed the McDonald summary, region classifications, PACS imports);
- its texts claimed **"MS diagnosis"**, offered a **"differential diagnosis"** tool and said new lesions "indicate disease activity"; **HIPAA compliance** was claimed without substantiation;
- its MS report tool sent `template` / `additional_findings`, which `/ai/report/generate` **silently drops** — every "comprehensive clinical report" was drafted from **no measurement**;
- SSE mode had **no authentication** (fastmcp 2.3.0 does not validate `Origin`), and responses carried **direct identifiers** to the model provider.

Also: a **"40 % CVS rule"** was shown as McDonald 2024 (it is not — verified wording in the CAPA), **≥1 PRL** was shown as a criterion met, reader provenance was **client-supplied**, and the longitudinal **activity candidate needed ≥2 lesions**, mis-attributed to MAGNIMS (MAGNIMS 2021: one suffices).

### Fixes
- `app/mcp/_backend.py`: the only backend client — GET, or POST to three compute-only, object-authorized routes; anything else refused **before** a request exists; identifiers removed from every response.
- Two read-only servers remain (`imaging`, `ms_clinical`), STDIO only; `segmentation`, `report`, `pacs` servers retired; texts bounded by the intended use.
- `/ai/report/generate` refuses (422) a request with no device measurement; the report panel explains why (en/es/de). HIPAA claims withdrawn.
- `lesion-annotations`: authenticated reader stored, statuses validated, counts per McDonald 2024, 40 % rule withdrawn (API, types, UI), PRL count neutral.
- `activity_candidate`: ≥1 new or enlarging candidate (MAGNIMS 2021).

pull_requests.head: fix/object-authorization-everywhere-capa009
pull_requests.body:
> **Stacked on #46 (CAPA-008).** This branch contains the CAPA-008 commit (`4d7b9a0`) plus CAPA-009 (`bbbaa6d`). Merge #46 first; the CAPA-009 diff is the last commit.

## What changed and why

**CAPA-009 (Critical)** — record: `docs/iec62304/records/capa/CAPA-009_Object_Authorization_Across_All_Routers.md`

1. **The patient check never executed (RC-026).** `require_patient_access` was a plain `def` returning a coroutine; FastAPI runs a plain-def dependency in a thread pool and never awaits what it returns. Any user with the role permission reached **every patient record** (get/update/delete, care team, history, documents by patient). A request probe as an unentitled radiologist showed the authorization ran **0 times** and the handler reached the data service; after the fix it runs once and answers 404. RC-026 had been "verified" by matching source text.
2. **~40 routes authorized no object**, including signed download links for any instance/study/document, any expert mask, any patient's study list, FHIR Patient/ImagingStudy, MRN enumeration, uploads/imports/AI and tool jobs on any patient, anyone's task/upload/import handle, an overlay of another patient's mask, and a raw client storage path used as a bucket key.
3. **SSRF:** any user could create/delete/test PACS connections to any URL. Websocket connection statistics of other users were readable.

### Fixes
- `require_patient_access` / `require_imaging_access` → `async def`.
- Path dependencies (`require_instance_access`, `require_study_access`, `require_patient_access`, `require_document_access`, new `require_version_access`); body/lookup checks (`authorize_patient_id`, `authorize_study_id`, `authorize_document_id`).
- AI and clinical-tool inputs authorized, required to belong to one patient matching any `patient_id`/`study_id`, passed to services as parsed, authorized paths.
- New `app/security/ownership.py` initiator registry: task, upload and import handles usable only by their initiator or an admin; unknown → 404.
- PACS connection create/delete/test and websocket stats → ADMIN only (listing connections stays open, credentials masked).

## Traceability
- Implements **REQ-SEC-014/015/016** (existing) and new **REQ-SEC-019, REQ-SEC-020** (SRS v1.4)
- Risk control **RC-036** for **HAZ-010** (RMF v1.6); **RC-026 erratum** recorded; TM v1.3
- Completes **CAPA-007 PA-7.2**; supersedes **CAPA-008 CA-8.8**

## Verification
- `test_capa009_object_authorization_everywhere.py`: **47 passed** — every mounted route referencing an object is classified and its mechanism re-derived from the code (new unclassified routes fail the build); 33 requests by an unentitled user → 404 before any data service; 4 admin-only routes → 403; positive controls (entitled caller passes; AI service receives the authorized path); no dependency can silently skip itself again.
- Full backend unit suite: **1200 passed** (no cloud credentials, as in CI). Adapted: `test_conformal_route.py` (fake image check returns a reference like the real one).
- **Negative controls: 32/32 detected** (`scripts/safety/capa009_negative_controls.py`, record `CAPA-009_negative_controls_2026-10-17.json`), incl. re-introducing the un-awaited patient dependency (7 failed).

## Not verified / owner decisions
- Production behaviour (needs two real accounts after deploy).
- UI handling of the new 403 for non-admins creating PACS connections.
- PA-9.3 re-verify every control whose evidence is source-text matching; PA-9.4 access-log review.

Research only (no device code). Fixes the two reviewer-fatal flaws found in the publication-strategy review.

**1. Training-set contamination.** FLAMeS was trained on 20 of the 30 Ljubljana (open_ms_data) scans. The exact 20 (patients 01–15, 21–25) were identified by matching against the arrays shipped with the public FLAMeS weights: all 20 match exactly. Every FLAMeS-on-Ljubljana number is now labelled training data. Each analysis is repeated on the 10 clean scans (n = 10, stated). Patient calibrations come from MSLesSeg only. A segmenter × cohort overlap table cites its sources.

**2. Healthy-control interval.** The interval was computed on 0/200 split-repeats; it is now computed on **0/30 distinct scans → 95 % upper bound 9.5 %** (verified in code). Other figures that counted repeated splits as new scans were corrected too: 40/200 → 5/30 and 17/200 → 2/30.

**Also:**
- Three baselines, computed on cached scores (CPU):
  - one candidate per scan (Dunn–Wasserman–Ramdas);
  - per-scan conformal risk control / Learn-then-Test;
  - hierarchical e-values (Lee & Ren 2025).
- Per-cohort AUROC.
- The scan ICC is confirmed by code.
- The v0.1 records reproduce identically.

**Weakened or withdrawn:**
- cross-site transport becomes "compatible, not demonstrated" (n = 10);
- the 1.8 % bound, "7–13×" and "0.75–0.82" are withdrawn.

**Still TODO:**
- a fully clean segmenter (needs a GPU);
- 70 more SibBMS controls (licence to confirm);
- confirm the ISBI rater mask;
- references marked "verify".

pull_requests.title: fix(clinical-tools): tool masks in the voxel order their marker declares; fail closed (CAPA-011, RC-039, HAZ-006) — merge after #52
pull_requests.head: fix/tool-runner-mask-axes-capa011

comments.author: nicolasbonilla
comments.body: Contenido unido a main dentro de la publicación firmada por el propietario #64 (commit 70cc5c7). Se cierra porque su rama base era intermedia.

pull_requests.body:
> **Merge after #52** (CAPA-010). This PR is based on `fix/viewer-safety-capa010`; rebased onto its latest head (`8b839fd`); two CAPA-011 commits: the fix, and the pre-merge-review grid check. Identifiers renumbered: **RC-039** (was RC-038) and **REQ-SAFE-028** (was REQ-SAFE-025), which CAPA-010 uses. Documents build on CAPA-010's versions: **SRS 1.6, RMF 1.8, TM 1.5**.

## What changed and why

**CAPA-011 (Critical) — clinical-tool masks were transposed twice on load.**

`ToolRunnerService._store_nifti_as_segmentation` (main: `tool_runner_service.py:883-885`, `:924`, transpose at `:829-831`) brought the tool's mask into the app's internal order (k, a0, a1) and stored **that** array under the RC-031 v2 marker, which declares "MRI-native (a0, a1, k)". The loader (`segmentation_service.py:874-879`, called at `:1167`) applied the (2,0,1) transpose a second time, so the axes came back swapped:

- non-cubic volume: wrong shape on load ((9, 4, 6) instead of (4, 6, 9));
- cubic volume: same shape, wrong place, **silent** — a lesion at MRI voxel (5, 1, 4) loaded at (4, 5, 1).

Affected every mask stored through the tool runner: **FLAMeS, LST-AI (types mask), SynthSeg, mindGlide (lesion and structure)**. Consequences: overlay in the wrong place (2D and 3D), lesion position and MAGNIMS region/DIS wrong. Also: the stored affine did not describe the stored array after reorientation, and the RC-031 "fail-safe" stored a mask whose position could not be established (legacy in-plane-transposed order).

**Fix** (`backend/app/services/tool_runner_service.py` only; no Class C module from `CLAUDE.md` touched; `segmentation_service.py` unchanged):
- new `_orient_mask_for_storage` → (array, affine): the mask reoriented onto the reference MRI's voxel order by affine (RC-031), with the affine of that array; stored under the v2 marker;
- the internal mask used for counts/shape is the loader's own decode (`SegmentationService._nifti_native_to_internal`); the marker comes from the shared constant, not a literal; `_orient_mask_to_display` derives from the same helper;
- **fails closed**: when the reference image is not passed, missing or unreadable, or the affine cannot place the mask, **nothing is stored** (no mask object, no segmentation record); the refusal is logged (`[RC-039] Clinical-tool mask NOT stored`) and raised as `SegmentationException` `TOOL_MASK_REFERENCE_UNAVAILABLE`, so the tool's task ends **FAILED** with "The tool's segmentation was not stored: … (RC-039). Re-run the tool." The legacy-order fallback is removed.
- **same grid required** (pre-merge review blocker): after reorientation the mask must have the image's array shape and a voxel-to-scanner transform equal to the image's within 0.001 in every element; otherwise nothing is stored, the task ends FAILED with `TOOL_MASK_GRID_MISMATCH` ("… not on the grid of the image it was computed on … The tool must return its result on the image's own grid."). Reproduced first: a 20×20×30 mask at 1 mm over a 40×40×10 study was stored and the task ended completed. Note: SynthSeg returns 1 mm, so its sidecar must resample back to the input grid, or its results on non-1 mm studies will be refused (PA-11.4).

Existing tests adapted to the fail-closed rule: `test_rc031_ingest_orientation_fix.py` (`TestFailsSafeToLegacy` → `TestFailsClosed`), and `test_flames_integration.py` / `test_clinical_tool_empty_mask.py` now pass the (required) reference image.

**Exposure:** the four tools are off in production (config defaults False; live services set no `*_ENABLED`, verified by the requester; no cloud command run here). Window: 2026-08-19 (`7fcf1cd`/`e1aea68`) → this fix. **No data migrated**; a read-only check is proposed (CAPA-011 §6, PA-11.2, owner decision).

**Open finding for the owner (CAPA-011 Finding 7, PA-11.5 — not implemented here):** `docker-compose.yml` enables LST-AI, SynthSeg and mindGlide (FLAMeS not) and sets no storage target, so the production defaults apply (bucket `brain-mri-medical-images` in `config.py`, Firestore project `brain-mri-476110` in `firebase.py`; it mounts `backend/credentials.json`). A development environment must not write to production. Proposed: separate dev project/bucket + dev service account via env (`GCS_BUCKET_NAME`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`), a start-up guard refusing production storage outside `ENVIRONMENT=production`, and no production defaults in code.

**Other V2 writers:** only `SegmentationService._save_masks_to_gcs` (correct, `_internal_to_nifti_native`). Local fallback writes unmarked legacy (consistent); `flames-worker` writes an untagged staging file re-stored by the tool runner; upload scripts go through the API.

## Requirement / risk IDs

- Implements **REQ-SAFE-028** (new, SRS 1.6); related REQ-FUNC-034/035.
- Risk control **RC-039** (new, RMF 1.8) for **HAZ-006** (primary), **HAZ-001**, **HAZ-005** (and through regions, HAZ-008). Erratum to RC-031 (still unregistered, CAPA-006 PA-6.6).

## Test evidence

- `backend/tests/unit/test_rc039_tool_runner_mask_axes.py` — 28 `test_rc039_*` cases, through the **real store path** and the **real load path** (`SegmentationService.get_mask` → `_load_segmentation` → `_load_masks_from_gcs`) on a non-cubic asymmetric volume (6×9×4) with a flipped, anisotropic, translated affine and one marked voxel. Asserts the same voxel (a0, a1, k), the same scanner position, the same slice layout, and the same position in the stored file served to the 3D viewer. Also: cubic silent case (5,1,4); tool output in another voxel order; LST-AI types mask; marker/order contract; **every tool end to end** through its real `_execute_*` (FLAMeS, LST-AI, SynthSeg, mindGlide lesion + structure), each in the MRI grid and in another voxel order; **fail closed**: no / missing / unreadable reference and indeterminate affine → error, nothing stored; each tool's run with an unreadable reference → FAILED, nothing stored; **same grid**: other shape, 0.5 mm shift, SynthSeg-like 1 mm output, and a SynthSeg run end to end → refused, nothing stored; float rounding accepted (positive control); **stored record**: `image_shape` = [a0, a1, k], `annotated_voxels`, agreement with the loaded mask (closes the review's surviving mutation).
- **On main: the 14 round-trip cases fail** (e.g. "lesion loaded at internal [(1, 4, 5)]; it was computed at MRI voxel (a0,a1,k)=(5,1,4) -> internal (4, 5, 1)"). **On the first fix (pre-rebase commit `a623671`): the 8 fail-closed cases fail** (mask stored; tool run COMPLETED; indeterminate affine crashed in nibabel with an unclear error). **The 4 grid cases fail before the grid check.** **Now: 28 passed.**
- `tests/unit`: **1249 passed**, 0 failed (rebased on CAPA-010 `8b839fd`). Manifest gate 222 passed; `-k test_rc` 426 passed.

## What and why

| 1 | No patient identity in the 3D view nor in the multi-panel view | A 3D brain or 2–4 sequences side by side with no name, no MRN, no "not identified" warning | `ImageViewer3D` and every `MultiPanelViewer` cell render `ViewportSafetyOverlay`; `ViewerApp` passes the identity; each panel shows its own image's orientation |
| 2 | 3D crosshair and bounding box of the selected lesion transposed | Marker at voxel (j, i) instead of (i, j) — elsewhere in the slice, possibly across the midline — while 2D was right | One shared mapping `lesionVoxelToNifti(z, y, x) = (y, x, z)` for crosshair and box |
| 3 | Ruler ×zoom; angle in pixel units | 10 mm read "20.0 mm" at zoom ×2 (×4 at zoom 4), ROI ×4 area, a 63.4° angle read "45.0°", rulers detached from the anatomy on zoom/pan | Overlay maps through the canvas transform (s0·zoom, centre·(1−zoom)+pan); angle in mm per axis |

| 5 | 3D orientation cube and niivue default slice letters (L/A), contrary to RC-023 | Laterality letters in 3D although no axis→screen mapping is verified | `isOrientCube: false`, `isOrientationTextVisible: false` on every 3D niivue instance |
