pull_requests.body:
**DRAFT — do not merge. Merge after #52 and #51** (they reserve RC-037/038/039, REQ-SAFE-025..028, SRS 1.5/1.6, RMF 1.7/1.8, TM 1.4/1.5). Feature flag `VITE_ENABLE_BROWSER_FLAMES` stays **OFF** by default (checked in the production build). Nothing deployed; no gcloud/firebase command run. Every approval field: **PENDING owner approval**.

## What and why

In-browser FLAMeS (CP-FLAMES-BROWSER-001): runs the FLAMeS nnU-Net model (Zenodo 17955359 v2.0, CC BY 4.0) in the clinician's browser with ONNX Runtime Web, so AI lesion drafts need no GPU server. This revision answers **both** adversarial reviews; point-by-point in `docs/research/flames-in-browser/REVIEW-RESPONSE.md` (§1–7 first review, **§8 re-review 2**).

### Re-review 2 ("do not merge yet", on c838bb1)

| # | Finding | Fix | Requirement / control / hazard |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | FLAIR gate does not generalise: on ISBI-2015 the full gate accepted **10 of 19** skull-stripped T1 as FLAIR; "136/151" was quoted for the gate but was the contrast part alone (full gate: **112/151**) | **`flair-gate/2`, fail closed.** Leave-one-dataset-out (MSLesSeg, open_ms_data, ISBI-2015) proved content alone cannot guarantee it, so the image content and the header can now only **refuse**; a FLAIR is accepted only with **positive evidence**: the clinician's explicit per-file confirmation of the sequence before each run (checkbox; recorded with the draft as `sequence_evidence=clinician`, the server records `sequence_confirmed_by` from the authenticated user) or a header with a FLAIR inversion time (≥ 1400 ms; a "FLAIR" label alone is not proof). Content re-fitted on all three sets (T1 rule 0.915, new grey-matter-class T1 rule ≤ 27 %, T2 rule ≤ 2.5 %). All numbers corrected | REQ-SAFE-033 (b)(c) · RC-049 · HAZ-001 |
| R2 | Radiologist confirmation not bound to the mask (technician replaced the mask; record still "reviewed by dr_rev") | Confirmation records `reviewed_mask_sha256` = SHA-256 of the exact stored mask; the client sends the SHA-256 of the mask on screen, 409 unless equal. **Any mask change resets the review to unreviewed** at the service's single save point (`enforce_review_binding` in `_save_segmentation`), so every write path is covered; the mask upload reports `ai_review_reset`. **No confirm button while there are unsaved corrections** ("save them first"); after saving corrections the app re-reads the provenance (fail safe: unreviewed) | REQ-SAFE-030 (d)(e) · RC-047 · HAZ-001 |
| R3 | `provenanceRecorded` accepted another model hash or an already "confirmed" echo | The echo must match exactly (model name, version, SHA-256, fold, source checkpoint, pipeline, sequence evidence) and be unreviewed with no reviewer / time / mask hash; otherwise the record is deleted and the save fails | REQ-SAFE-030 (c) · RC-047 |

### First review (unchanged, see REVIEW-RESPONSE §1–7)
Skull clues (a FLAIR with skull and zero background passed the old gate; now 12/12 refused), explicit empty result, no autosave of AI drafts, AI provenance stored, unsaved work never discarded, model SHA-256 tested on download and cache paths, licences reachable, COOP/COEP impact analysis (`firebase.json` unchanged; single-thread duration shown, cancel safe), IEC 62304 records (SRS 1.7, RMF 1.9, TM 1.6, SOUP 1.2, CMP 1.1 — drafts).

Class C modules listed in CLAUDE.md are **not** modified. Backend changes are confined to `schemas.py`, `segmentation_service.py` (create, `mask_sha256`, `enforce_review_binding`, `_save_segmentation`) and `routes/segmentation.py` (create, `ai-review/confirm`, mask PUT).

## FLAIR gate — corrected numbers (`FLAIR-GATE-VALIDATION.md`)

**Leave-one-dataset-out** (thresholds fitted on the other two sets; every case treated as if the clinician had confirmed it — i.e. the content check as second barrier):

| Held out | FLAIR accepted (full gate) | non-FLAIR refused (full gate) | let through |
|---|---|---|---|
| ISBI-2015 | 12/19 · 0.63 [0.41–0.81] | 18/19 · 0.95 [0.75–0.99] | case007 T1 |
| MSLesSeg | 70/115 · 0.61 [0.52–0.69] | 229/230 · 0.996 [0.98–1.00] | P71_T2 |
| open_ms_data | 35/36 · 0.97 [0.86–0.99] | 102/102 · 1.00 [0.96–1.00] | — |

**Shipped `flair-gate/2` on all 533 public volumes** (replay of the shipped decision code; reproduced from the committed evidence files):
* without positive evidence: **0/170 FLAIR and 0/351 non-FLAIR accepted** (fails closed);
* with the clinician's confirmation (apparent, in-sample): FLAIR **87/170** accepted (ISBI 12/19, MSLesSeg 40/115, open_ms 35/36); non-FLAIR **351/351** refused; with skull **12/12** refused.
* Old gate, corrected: complete `flair-gate/1` accepted **112/151** FLAIR (136/151 was the contrast part alone), refused 343/344 non-FLAIR, and accepted **10/19** ISBI-2015 T1.

Honest limits: acceptance relies on a human confirmation; the content barrier is not guaranteed on an unseen scanner; about half of genuine FLAIRs are refused (safe failure, usability cost).

## Test evidence

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Frontend suite (`npx vitest run --pool=threads`) | **236 passed**, 3 skipped (opt-in parity / gate-validation / replay harnesses) |
| Type check (`tsc --noEmit`) | clean |

| Backend unit suite | **1307 passed** (incl. `test_rc047_ai_draft_provenance.py` 12 tests, CAPA-009 route classification, risk-control manifest gate) |
| Negative controls (`research/flames_in_browser/negative_controls_v2.py`, all re-run on this code) | **45/46 mutations detected** (H1–H10, I1–I2, G1–G9+G5b, F1, B1–B10, U1–U5, P1–P2, E1–E6); G6 (local normalisation removed) not detectable with phantoms — recorded. Code as reviewed (d81cb78 and c838bb1) fails the new tests **6/6** — `docs/iec62304/records/risk_verification/CP-FLAMES-BROWSER-001_negative_controls_2026-10-17.json` |

Semantic: `useSegmentationStore` (new `maskDigestCallback`, `hasUnsavedMaskChanges`).

- Whether a clinician's per-file confirmation is acceptable as the positive evidence for the sequence (its usability belongs to CA-FLAMES-4), and whether refusing about half of genuine FLAIRs is acceptable.

pull_requests.title: research(paper-a): v0.3 pre-registered five-cohort audit (thick-slice sites, 5-fold ensemble, segmenter shift)
pull_requests.head: research/paper-a-v0.3
pull_requests.body:
## What changed and why

Research only — **not the medical device**; no file under `backend/`, `frontend/` or any Class C module is touched. Stacks on #48 (Paper A v0.2, still a draft); the diff to `main` therefore includes the v0.2 commits.

Paper A v0.3: a **pre-registered** five-cohort audit of conformal lesion-level false-discovery control on FLAMeS, run on the local CPU from the fold-by-fold FLAMeS maps of the October cloud run (no cloud command).

- `docs/research/paper/PROTOCOL-v0.3.md` — committed before any outcome (9951494); implementation clarifications and one gate deviation logged before outcomes (c0c5fa1, 50c9b08); a transparency note after the results.
- `research/paper_a/v03_*.py` — inventory (SHA-256 of every input), candidate extraction + gate G1 (fold-0 pipeline reproduces v0.2's labels 4400/4400), metrics, analysis, labelled post-hoc checks; `test_v03_metrics.py` (33 tests pass).
- `docs/research/records/2026-10-21_paper_a_v03_*` — all numbers.
- `docs/research/paper/RESULTS-v0.3.md`, updated `manuscript-draft.md` (v0.3), and `APP-FEATURE-slice-thickness-reliability.md` (research input, **not a requirement**).

## Key results (ensemble arm, 304 scans / 245 patients)

- Conformal BH (P1) **not violated in any of 16 held-out-site cells**; 1-mm → thick-slice transport is *inconclusive* by the pre-registered rule (Muslim α = 0.1: 0.122 [0.062, 0.197]).
- Per-scan FDX threshold (P2) **refuted** for 1-mm → thick slices (21 % / 29 % of scans above γ vs 10 %); site-only recalibration with ≥ 10 patients restores it, adding site patients to the foreign pool does not.
- With slice thickness the slack shrinks (realised FDR at α = 0.2: 0.018 → 0.120) and raw detection of small lesions falls (50 % detection needs ≥ 50 mm³ on 4.5–8.3 mm slices; 80 % never reached on 2D slices).
- The **5-fold ensemble** raises candidate AUROC 0.67–0.76 → 0.78–0.82, doubles sensitivity at the guarantee, and removes the fold-0 (v0.2 pipeline) violations on MS3SEG.
- Same-image segmenter swap (LST-AI-calibrated, FLAMeS-tested) **violates** the guarantee (0.207 at α = 0.1).

Limitations stated: estimated Muslim pixel size, 9 PediMS children, contamination handling (20 Ljubljana scans excluded), site/thickness/annotation confounding.

Requirement / hazard: none — research input only; the app spec must go through SRS/RMF before any implementation.

## Addendum 2026-10-24 — 100 healthy controls (separately pre-registered)

- `docs/research/paper/PROTOCOL-v0.3-addendum-controls.md` committed **before any control outcome** (caa47e7): contamination check (SibBMS is not in FLAMeS training — FLAMeS Table 1, Zenodo card, 668-entry weight fingerprint, release dates), frozen operating points from patient data only, primary endpoint, decision rules for paper and app.
- `research/paper_a/v03c_{inventory,calibration,controls,controls_check}.py` + records `docs/research/records/2026-10-24_paper_a_v03c_*` (413f5b5). An independent re-implementation reproduced every count exactly.
- **Results** (ensemble, 1-mm-site calibration; controls with ≥ 1 reported lesion of 100, exact 95 % CI): conformal BH α = 0.1 **14 [7.9, 22.4]** and α = 0.2 **24 [16.0, 33.6]** — both *inconclusive*, above nominal; per-scan threshold 6 [2.2, 12.6] *holds* (but finds almost nothing in patients); **fold 0 violated** (59/100 at α = 0.1). Without selection: ≥ 1 lesion in **85/100** healthy brains, and the app's brain-DIS rule met in **19/100 [11.8, 28.1]** (0–3/100 after selection). False lesions are deep (2/263 near the skull-strip edge), 63 % periventricular.
- Manuscript / RESULTS / app spec updated (f3b22cd): the old "0/200 (≤ 1.8 %)" and "0/30 (≤ 9.5 %)" healthy-DIS statements are withdrawn; the app spec now says the dial is "not validated on healthy brains" and adds a rule never to compute DIS from an unreviewed automatic segmentation (owner problem report / risk review proposed; no app code changed).
- Limits: one site, template-normalised images, "lesion-free" assumed (not expert-read), licence CC BY-NC-SA (research only). LST-AI control arm pending (TODO).

pull_requests.title: research(lesion-detector): pre-registered v3 (not met), v3.1 (met; gain mostly = 5-fold ensemble), v3.2 healthy controls (not met; confounded)
pull_requests.head: research/lesion-detector-v3
pull_requests.body:
## What changed and why

Research only — pre-registered lesion-level false-positive detector for the CALM-MS precision dial (v3 and v3.1). **No product code is touched** (`backend/app`, `frontend` unchanged; no Class C module modified). Everything lives in `research/lesion_detector_v3/`, `docs/research/lesion-detector-v3/` and `docs/research/records/`.

The conformal lesion-selection guarantee has low power because raw FLAMeS probability separates true from false candidate lesions poorly. v3/v3.1 test new candidate-level features, each with a protocol committed before any result was computed.

**v3 (2026-10-17): pre-registered criterion NOT met.**
- Primary: pooled leave-one-cohort-out AUROC, MSLesSeg ↔ clean Ljubljana-10.
- Result: Δ +0.014 [−0.012, +0.041] vs raw probability.
- Gains appear within a single domain, but the FLAIR features carry a strong site signature (cohort-identity AUROC 0.98).

**v3.1 (2026-10-21): pre-registered criterion MET on three never-analysed sites (MS3SEG, Muslim, PediMS).**
- New features: 5-fold FLAMeS disagreement and LST-AI agreement.
- Pooled external AUROC 0.832 vs 0.721 raw, Δ +0.111 [+0.096, +0.125].
- Δ vs the plain 5-fold ensemble: +0.044 [+0.037, +0.051].
- Fold disagreement shows no site signature (cohort-identity AUROC 0.502). LST-AI agreement still does (0.637).

**Post-hoc, labelled as such:** with candidates defined on the 5-fold mean map (how FLAMeS is deployed), the ensemble mean already reaches 0.796, and the learned model adds only +0.013 [+0.008, +0.018]. Most of the registered gain is the effect of using the 5-fold ensemble.

**v3.2 (2026-10-24): 100 SibBMS healthy controls — pre-registered criterion NOT met; confound found.**
- Pre-registered in 3c24977 before any control feature or score; code and deviation D1 in 6606cc6 before the run; results in 90797a9.
- Candidates from the 5-fold mean map; subject-disjoint 5-fold cross-fit (MS patients and controls); the three unseen MS sites held out as in v3.1.
- Primary (real 1-mm MS lesions vs healthy-control candidates): model trained with controls 0.822 vs ensemble mean 0.805, Δ +0.017 [+0.005, +0.030] — below the 0.05 threshold.
- False candidates per healthy scan at 90 % sensitivity: ensemble 1.02 [0.72, 1.35], trained-with-controls 0.97 (Δ −0.05 [−0.13, +0.09]) — not met. The v3.1 detector is worse here: 1.31 (Δ +0.29 [+0.13, +0.41]).
- Unseen MS sites: non-inferior and unchanged (0.810 vs 0.809).
- Confound: among false candidates, controls are recognised with AUROC 0.848 (two MS sites: 0.55); a controls-only model falls to 0.650 on MS false candidates; a pure cohort probe reaches 0.833 on the primary endpoint. Confound gate failed.
- Fold disagreement alone separates lesions from healthy-control candidates (0.852 vs 0.805), but site vs healthy status cannot be separated with one site.
- Gate V1 reproduces v3.1 and paper A's control candidates exactly; independent re-implementation (K6) matches.
- App consequence: keep the 5-fold ensemble + disagreement; no learned re-scorer; no healthy-brain specificity claim. Next: SibBMS MS patients (same site) to de-confound.

Full write-ups: `docs/research/lesion-detector-v3/RESULTS.md`, `RESULTS-v3.1.md` and `RESULTS-v3.2.md`. Protocols and deviation logs: `PROTOCOL.md`, `PROTOCOL-v3.1.md` and `PROTOCOL-v3.2.md`.

## Traceability

- Related investigational requirement: REQ-FUNC-CALM-001 (feature stays dark). This PR does not implement or change any requirement.
- No hazard control changed (HAZ-CALM-1..8 unaffected).
- Nothing here may be wired to the guarantee path without a separate pre-registered validation and code review.

## Checks

- 13 unit tests: `python -m pytest research/lesion_detector_v3/test_features_v3.py`.
- Feature code takes no ground truth (unit-tested).
- Train, calibration and test patients are asserted disjoint in every split.
- Input SHA-256 values are recorded in the `*_feature_cache_meta.json` records.
- v3.2: control inputs hashed in `2026-10-24_lesion_detector_v32_inventory.json`; independent re-implementation in `check_v32_independent.py` (record `..._v32_independent_check.json`).

Draft: for review only, do not merge without code review.

Research code (not the medical device; `research/` is outside the IEC 62304 scope). Prepares — **does not launch** — a GPU fine-tuning study that teaches FLAMeS to read thick-slice 2D FLAIR, following Paper A v0.3 (PR #54: on real 4.5–8 mm sites 50 % lesion detection needs ≥ 50 mm³ vs ≥ 14 mm³ at 1 mm, and the per-scan guarantee breaks) and the super-resolution study's recommendation (MindGlide recipe: random slice thickening in training instead of SR).

- `docs/research/flames-thick/PROTOCOL.md` — **pre-registered, committed first (5b286f2) before any code or run**: arms R (FLAMeS fold 0), A (FLAMeS-thick), B (same fine-tuning without thickening, control), E (5-fold ensemble, context); MSLesSeg-TRAIN-only training with a hard-coded guard; augmentation law; 211-scan evaluation set; outcomes copied from Paper A v0.3; decision rules (H1 co-primary: lesion-wise F1 ΔCI > 0 and ≥ +0.03 with false-lesions ratio CI ≤ 1.10 on MS3SEG+Muslim+PediMS; H2 1-mm non-inferiority Dice −0.02 / F1 −0.03 with a Ljubljana guard-rail).
- `docs/research/flames-thick/RUNBOOK.md` — exact commands, GPU choice, pilot (≤ 2 USD worst case, ≈ 0.2 USD expected) and full run (≈ 20 USD, 16–31 USD range), pass/fail checks, failure table.
- `research/flames_thick/` — thick-slice simulator (`thick_slice.py`, numpy) and its batchgeneratorsv2 transform; nnU-Net 2.8.1 trainers `nnUNetTrainerFLAMeSThick` / `nnUNetTrainerFLAMeSFT` (strict load of **all** FLAMeS weights incl. heads, refuse random init, warm-up + poly LR, checkpoint callbacks, cost-guard hook); data prep (MSLesSeg train only, FLAMeS plans transferred, patient-grouped split); Vertex AI container entry point (Spot attempts, SHA-256-checked inputs, resume from the bucket, in-pilot SIGKILL + resume test, cumulative cost guard, model export, ledger records); Dockerfile (Ubuntu 22.04 digest-pinned, Python 3.10.12, the v2 lock with torch 2.14.1+cu126); evaluation-set selection; pre-registered analysis; pilot report.
- `research/cloud/`: `launch_vertex.py` (dry run by default; `--submit` only for the coordinator, refuses other projects/images/buckets), `pricing.py` (Vertex AI Spot training priced from Compute Engine Spot SKUs; Vertex service id left as a TODO), `build_ledger.py` (reads Vertex training and evaluation runs), `flames_ensemble_driver.py` (`--model TAG=FOLDER`, unchanged without it), `vm_flames_thick_eval.sh` (CPU evaluation VM with the v2 conventions).

## GPU choice
Spot custom-training quota only (Compute Engine GPU quota is 0). **T4 on n1-standard-8**: 0.4276 USD/h (catalogue 2026-10-18), est. 195–310 s/epoch → 0.023–0.037 USD/epoch; A100 ties within uncertainty (2.2273 USD/h, 44–66 s/epoch) but is harder to get as Spot and its 12-vCPU host risks starving the GPU. The pilot measures it; the pre-registered rule switches to the A100 only if > 15 % cheaper per epoch.

## Tests (local, CPU; torch 2.14.1 + nnunetv2 2.8.1)
- 97 unit tests pass (`research/flames_thick/tests`, `research/cloud/tests`): simulator physics (slab width = thickness, Gaussian FWHM, gaps never seen, no shift, mean kept), label untouched and never read, 2/3 application rate, insertion after nnU-Net's spatial transform with a full pipeline pass on the real patch size, axis mapping (MSLesSeg axial = patch axis 1), LR schedule, external trainer lookup, data guard, split, cost guard, Vertex pricing, dry-run request, launcher refusals, ledger rows, evaluation set, analysis rules on a synthetic 211-scan cohort, pilot projection.
- `test_e2e_local.py` (opt-in, 3 pass in 10 min): the container code path on CPU with the real FLAMeS fold-0 weights and 3 real MSLesSeg-train scans (+ a test scan correctly ignored), a local folder as the bucket — strict init (292 tensors), FLAMeS plans + preprocessing, thick augmentation inside nnU-Net, checkpoint upload, **SIGKILL after epoch 0 and resume at epoch 1 from the bucket**, validation (Dice 0.79), model export, ledger records, exported model through the evaluation predictor, cost guard stopping cleanly. Record: `docs/research/records/2026-10-21_flames_thick_local_e2e_output.txt`. Local-only deviation: 64³ patch (a 16-GB laptop cannot back-propagate the real patch on CPU; refused on GPU).
- Not testable locally: the CUDA image build, Vertex Spot scheduling/restarts, GCS — that is what the pilot is for.

## Finding while preparing
MSLesSeg's own `info_dataset/patient_scanners_info_FLAIR.csv` gives the native FLAIR slice thickness: 2–5 mm (train: 31 at 2–2.3 mm, 49 at 3 mm, 8 at 4–5 mm; test: 7 of 22 at 4–5 mm). MSLesSeg is "1-mm-delivered" (MNI), not 1-mm acquired — relevant to Paper A's band B1. The Figshare record also has `MSLesSeg_RAW.zip` (native space).

Nothing was launched, built or pushed to any cloud project. Requirement/hazard IDs: not applicable (research, not device software).

pull_requests.title: feat(lesions): reliability by slice thickness card — Paper A v0.3 (CP-SLICE-THICKNESS-001, DRAFT, flag OFF; merge after #52, #51, #53)
pull_requests.head: feat/slice-thickness-reliability
pull_requests.body:
## What

A **"reliability by slice thickness"** card next to the lesion results (inside the lesion dashboard, above the lesion table), behind the feature flag `VITE_ENABLE_SLICE_THICKNESS_RELIABILITY`, **OFF by default**. Change ID **CP-SLICE-THICKNESS-001**. Research input: Paper A v0.3 (PR #54, `docs/research/paper/APP-FEATURE-slice-thickness-reliability.md` on `research/paper-a-v0.3` — a research input, not a requirement).

For the image the segmentation was drawn on, the card shows:

- the **slice thickness of the original acquisition and how it is known**: from the DICOM acquisition header ("6.5 mm, from the acquisition header of …"), as a lower bound from the image grid ("at least 6 mm …; may be thicker"), or **"Not determinable"** with the reason (e.g. "registered to a template grid (MNI 1 mm); the original slice thickness is not recorded");
- the **thickness band** and, from the versioned evidence, **from which lesion size lesions were found 8 times in 10 and half of the time** (worst case over the band's evidence rows), plus the per-size detection table with its evidence size (scans / patients / sites) and a post-hoc marker;
- plain guidance: *an empty or short lesion list does not mean that there are no lesions*; on thick or unknown thickness *a 3D FLAIR (≤ 1.5 mm) is recommended for small lesions*;
- **no false-lesion rate, at any thickness**, with the reason (thick/unknown: not reliable without a ≥ 10-patient calibration from this site, none exists; thin: no calibration for the deployed segmenter);
- scope: research evidence (FLAMeS 5-fold ensemble), not validated for this site or for the segmenter that produced the list; not a diagnosis, not for McDonald counting, nothing for healthy/screening populations. English / Spanish / German, following the interface language.

## Why

Paper A v0.3 found that (1) a false-lesion guarantee calibrated on thin-slice data does not carry over to thick 2D FLAIR (2.6–3.2× the locally calibrated rate; the per-scan promise was refuted and is restored only with ≥ 10 local patients, at very low sensitivity) and (2) small-lesion detection drops with the **original** slice thickness (MSLesSeg, 14–50 mm³: 74 % at 2–2.3 mm, 65 % at 3 mm, 39 % at 4–5 mm **[post hoc]**; thick sites: no lesion size found 8 times in 10). MSLesSeg is delivered on a 1-mm grid although it was acquired at 2–5 mm, so the card must read the **original** thickness and must never take a fine grid for a thin acquisition. Project rule: every paper becomes a real feature of the app.

## How (minimum, safe)

- **Backend** (`app/services/acquisition_geometry.py` new; `imaging_service.py`; `schemas.py`): every loaded image now carries `metadata.acquisition_geometry` = `{state: native | at_least | not_determinable, effective_mm, source, reason, values read}`. `native` only from an ORIGINAL DICOM with the spacing between slices or a 3D acquisition (gap counted: larger of thickness and spacing). A NIfTI is never native: a grid coarser than 1.5 mm is a lower bound; a fine grid is not determinable (template grid named). Missing / invalid / contradictory / unreadable → not determinable — never a default (the legacy `slice_thickness` field is 1.0 mm by default and is never used). Total (never raises, so image loading cannot break). **The Class C utilities `nifti_utils.py` / `dicom_utils.py` are not modified** — their extractors are wrapped. No new endpoint.
- **Frontend**: `utils/sliceThicknessReliability.ts` (strict parse; the segmentation's own image, or the single original FLAIR of a processed image, named; thicker source wins; worst-case sizes), `config/sliceThicknessReliability.v1.json` (versioned evidence asset bound to commit `cabb99d` and the SHA-256 of both research records), `SliceThicknessReliabilityCard.tsx` (lazy, behind the flag), wiring in `LesionDashboard.tsx` / `ViewerApp.tsx`. With the flag ON the card may call the **existing**, authorized `/imaging/metadata` route for the segmentation's image (when it is not the image on screen) and for the original FLAIR of a processed image. With the flag OFF nothing of it is loaded or requested.
- No model change, no new endpoint, no cloud command, nothing deployed.

## Requirements, hazards, risk controls (all DRAFT — PENDING owner approval)

- **SRS 1.8**: REQ-FUNC-098 (card), REQ-FUNC-099 (geometry per image), REQ-SAFE-034 (thickness read, never assumed), REQ-SAFE-035 (no false-lesion rate without a ≥ 10-patient site calibration), REQ-SAFE-036 (figures from a versioned, source-bound asset; worst case).
- **RMF 1.10**: **HAZ-015** (new: the card states a thinner acquisition or better detection than the study supports, or a false-lesion rate that does not hold) with a *proposed* pre-control estimate S4/P3; HAZ-001 cause (thick slices: most small lesions missed) in §3.4; **RC-054..RC-058**; HAZ-015 residual **UNDETERMINED** → the feature stays OFF; open items in §7.2.
- **TM 1.7**: forward rows, safety addendum, test rows (UT-RC054, UT-STC-LOGIC, UI-STC-CARD, UT-STC-FLAG).
- **Manifest**: RC-054..RC-058 bound to their tests (inserted at the top of `controls` to avoid colliding with the entries #52/#51/#53 append).

**Merge after #52, #51 and #53** (they hold SRS 1.5–1.7, RMF 1.7–1.9, TM 1.4–1.6; expect trivial conflicts in the version lines and doc-control tables).

## Verification

- Backend unit suite: **1269 passed** (baseline 1200 + 34 `test_rc054_*` + 35 manifest checks for the new controls).
- Frontend suite (vitest `--pool=threads`): **158 passed** (baseline 116 + 42 new: `rc055`–`rc058`). `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Production build (`vite build`, `.env.production`, flag not set): the bundled env object has no `VITE_ENABLE_SLICE_THICKNESS_RELIABILITY`, the flag compiles to `En("ENABLE_SLICE_THICKNESS_RELIABILITY",!1)`, the card, logic and evidence asset live only in the lazy chunk `SliceThicknessReliabilityCard-*.js` — `records/risk_verification/CP-SLICE-THICKNESS-001_production_build_flag_check_2026-10-21.json`.
- **Negative controls** (`scripts/safety/slice_thickness_negative_controls.py`, one mutation at a time, anchors asserted unique, bytes restored and hash-checked): **35/35 detected** — RC-054 B1–B12 (12/12), RC-055 P1–P8 (8/8), RC-056 R1–R3 (3/3), RC-057 D1–D9 (9/9), RC-058 F1–F3 (3/3); restored: backend 34 / frontend 42 passed. **Provenance**: every figure, lesion, scan and patient count of the evidence asset re-derived from the research records at `cabb99d`; both SHA-256 match. Record: `records/risk_verification/CP-SLICE-THICKNESS-001_negative_controls_2026-10-21.json`.
- Not done: usability / radiologist review; re-derivation for the deployed segmenter; integration tests (no new route).

## What the owner must approve / decide

1. SRS 1.8, RMF 1.10 (incl. the new HAZ-015 and its proposed estimate), TM 1.7 — every approval field says *PENDING owner approval*.
2. Before the flag is turned ON anywhere: re-derive the evidence for the deployed segmenter version (and lock the asset version to it); radiologist review of the wording + usability (IEC 62366); keep the original DICOM geometry at PACS import (today the NIfTI conversion drops it, so most stored studies read "at least" or "not determinable"); the CALM-MS panel must apply RC-056 before it is ever enabled; safety class of the new modules (proposed: add them to the Class C list); register the evidence asset as a configuration item in CMP-001 (after #53).
3. Code review (Class C territory: it changes what a clinician is told about how far to trust the lesion overlay).

## Honest limits

- Research figures, one segmenter, bands confounded with site; three MSLesSeg rows are post hoc (marked on the card).
- NIfTI files never give a native thickness; "original" / "processed" / "FLAIR" rely on the viewer's existing filename conventions — a misnamed file can only yield "not determinable" or the single FLAIR-named original, which the card names for the reader to check.
- Not shown in the AI report (out of scope for this minimum change).

pull_requests.title: research(paper-c): pilot — per-patient guarantee on false new-lesion activity calls (pre-registered)
pull_requests.head: research/paper-c-pilot
pull_requests.body:
## What

Paper C pilot (research code, **not the medical device**; no app code changed): a per-patient,
distribution-free bound on FALSE "new/enlarging lesion" (disease-activity) calls between two FLAIR
timepoints, evaluated on public data only.

- `docs/research/paper-c/NOVELTY-CHECK.md` — focused re-search (arXiv API, Europe PMC, web). Still
  open as an application: no guarantee on patient-level false activity in longitudinal MS MRI;
  closest: McKinley 2020, Homssi 2023 (SDC, voxel-wise Neyman–Pearson), Conformal Triage 2024,
  MSSEG-2 measurements (Valencia 2022, Andresen 2022, Masson 2026). Statistics are not new.
- `PROTOCOL.md` — pre-registered (6233b4b) before any detector output; deviations logged.
- `RESULTS.md`, `manuscript-skeleton.md`, `APP-FEATURE.md` (research input only), `CLOUD-JOB.md`.
- `research/paper_c/` — inventory, FLAMeS-overlap check, detectors (model-free subtraction; the
  app's own `compare_timepoints` imported read-only), conformal thresholds (marginal, PAC,
  plug-in), analysis, 11 synthetic tests, separate-path verification of the primary cells.

## Why

MAGNIMS 2021: one new/enlarging lesion = activity. MSSEG-2 systems call false new lesions in
14–36 % of stable patients; nobody states a bound. MSSEG-2 needs an access agreement, so this is a
pilot on open_ms longitudinal (Lesjak 2016, CC-BY) and MSLesSeg (CC-BY-4.0).

## Results (pilot)

- **No stable patients** exist in either public set (20/20 and 25/25 active) → the measured
  quantity is the per-patient rate of ≥ 1 false new/enlarging call (equals false activity in a
  stable patient under a stated assumption).
- **Validity:** 4/4 primary cells, no violation detected — open_ms 0.10 [0.01, 0.32], 0.20
  [0.06, 0.44]; MSLesSeg 0.08 [0.01, 0.26], 0.20 [0.07, 0.41] at α = 0.1 / 0.2.
- **Utility:** at α = 0.2 only 0/20 and 5/25 patients flagged by a true change → pre-registered
  **NO-GO** (redesign the change score before MSSEG-2). FLAMeS probability change (secondary) 10/25.
- **The app's current `activity_candidate` rule** (on FLAMeS masks): ≥ 1 false new/enlarging
  candidate in 25/25 patients, 8.2 per patient (approximate truth).

## Pending

Cloud job (not launched; owner launches): FLAMeS 5 folds on the 40 open_ms longitudinal FLAIRs,
≈ 4 h, ≈ 0.7 USD list, project `mstool-research` only — see `CLOUD-JOB.md`. Arm A4 is
pre-registered and runs automatically after the download.

## Compliance notes

No requirement/hazard IDs: research only, nothing deployed, no app module modified (the Class C
list in CLAUDE.md is untouched). Disk: open_ms FLAIRs deleted after use (re-fetch with `--stream`).
Do not merge without review.

pull_requests.title: Research (paper D): fragility of automated dissemination-in-space decisions - pre-registered multiverse study
pull_requests.head: research/paper-d-dis-fragility
pull_requests.body:
## What and why

Paper D asks how often an **automated brain dissemination-in-space (DIS) decision** changes when only
plausible pipeline choices change — segmenter, probability threshold, minimum lesion size, region rule /
atlas, registration — measured against the DIS that **the device's own code** reports from an expert
lesion mask. Research code and documents only; **no `backend/app` file is changed**. The device's Class C
modules (`ms_region_classifier.py`, `lesion_analysis_service.py`, `lesion_metrics.py`) are imported
read-only and reproduced bit for bit.

Research input for **REQ-FUNC-052** (DIS), **REQ-FUNC-053** (MAGNIMS regions), **REQ-SAFE-015**; hazards
**HAZ-005** (wrong region) and **HAZ-008** (DIS display).

## Contents

- `docs/research/paper-d/PROTOCOL.md` — pre-registration, committed and pushed before any result (`980cb56`)
- `docs/research/paper-d/LITERATURE.md` — focused novelty check (all three novelty claims supported)
- `research/paper_d/` — grid code, LST-AI greedy registration reproduction, analysis, 16 tests
- `docs/research/paper-d/RESULTS.md` + `records/` — all pre-specified outcomes, deviations, post hoc items labelled
- `docs/research/paper-d/MANUSCRIPT.md` — skeleton with honest limitations
- `docs/research/paper-d/APP-FEATURE.md` — "DIS stability" indicator, **marked research input, not a requirement**

## Data

Public, stored locally and never versioned: MSLesSeg (CC-BY-4.0) and Ljubljana 3D MS DB (CC-BY), MNI 1 mm.
Ljubljana patients FLAMeS was trained on are excluded from primary analyses (sensitivity only). Primary
set: 124 scans, 85 patients. Atlas: LST-AI MSMask (repository MIT; atlas licence still to confirm, as in
CAPA-006 PA-6.5); no FSL atlas. No data of the device's users; no cloud resource.

## Key results (95 % patient-clustered bootstrap CIs)

| Outcome | Result |
|---|---|
| Device automated default vs expert-mask decision | 3.2 % (0.8–6.8) flipped |
| LST-AI as shipped | 8.1 % (3.3–13.8) |
| Mean over 1,120 plausible pipelines | 5.3 % (2.9–8.5) |
| Not unanimous across the 1,120 pipelines | **38.7 % (29.1–49.2)** — C1 met |
| Contested (10–90 % of pipelines) | 9.7 % (5.0–15.4) |
| Lowest lesion-count tertile: not unanimous | 65.1 % |
| Biggest driver | **segmenter** 7.3 % vs registration 4.0 % (diff 3.3, 1.2–5.6) — C3 met |
| Expert mask, only rule/size/registration varied | 4.8 % (1.5–9.2) not unanimous — C2 not met |
| Third ventricle counted as periventricular (LST-AI v1 + device MSMask path) | 0.08 % of expert lesions, 0 decisions — C5 not met |
| Pre-registered threshold/size/ventricle indicator | nearly blind (1/124); post hoc segmenter disagreement flags 11 %, incl. 3/4 default errors |

## Device findings — recommend a problem report (SPR-001) under HAZ-005; not fixed here (Class C)

1. MSMask label 4 contains the third ventricle, so the MSMask path assigns PV to lesions touching it —
   a nonconformity to REQ-FUNC-053 ("abutting the lateral ventricles") and Filippi 2019. Small effect here.
2. 6.3 % of expert lesions fall in no MSMask zone and are reported as deep white matter by default.
3. MSMask labels deep grey matter as white matter (guideline exception not applied).

## Verification

- Device zone map equal on all 144 scans; device counts and DIS equal on all 288 checked masks.
- `backend/venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest research/paper_d/tests -q` → 16 passed (device equality,
  literal port of LST-AI `annotate.py`, atlas facts).

## Limitations (stated in every document)

**No radiologist reads yet**: the reference is the device rule on an expert mask, not a radiologist's DIS.
The final paper requires **three neuroradiologists** (protocol §10). Established-MS population, brain only,
two single-site cohorts, LST-AI v2 (FastSurfer) not run.

Draft — do not merge or deploy.

pull_requests.head: qms/capa012-and-problem-reports
pull_requests.body:
**Documentation only. No code is modified. No approval is recorded anywhere: every approval field reads "PENDING owner approval".**

Merge order: **after #52, #51, #53, #59 and #49.** Based on `feat/flames-in-browser-on-capa011` (#52 + #51 + #53); contains PR #49 (SDP-001 v1.1), because CAPA-012 amends text that only exists there. IDs and versions continue after those PRs: RC-059..RC-062, REQ-SAFE-037 (RC-054..058 / REQ-SAFE-034..036 / REQ-FUNC-098..099 / HAZ-015 are reserved by #59); SRS 1.9, RMF 1.11, TM 1.8 (1.8 / 1.10 / 1.7 reserved by #59); SDP-001 1.2 (1.1 in #49). RMF §3.4 is reserved by #59, so the new section is §3.5.

## 1. CAPA-012 — approval and review records (process; IEC 62304 §5.1/§9, ISO 13485 §4.2.4/§4.2.5/§7.3)
`docs/iec62304/records/capa/CAPA-012_Approval_And_Review_Records.md` — severity **Major** (proposed; owner may raise to Critical).
- Facts (paper H, PR #57, re-checked read-only 2026-10-22): **0 formal GitHub reviews on 56 PRs**; **all 31 lines** recording the owner's approval in 19 controlled documents were written by the agent in 5 agent-trailered commits, transcribing chat approvals; `main` is **not protected** (API: "Branch not protected", no rulesets); the only code owner is the PR author, so the required review cannot be given; the agent works under the owner's git identity and GitHub account; no commit is signed by the owner's key. The agent harness refused to write such lines on 2026-10-17 to 2026-10-21 (correct behaviour, not a QMS control).
- Proposed actions: CA-12.1 approvals recorded by the owner himself (signed owner sign-off commit without the agent trailer, or a formal review from the owner's account on PRs authored by a separate agent identity); CA-12.2 a review record per PR (independent adversarial review report + owner decision); CA-12.3 branch protection and a separate agent identity; CA-12.4 correct documents that describe controls that do not exist; CA-12.5 independent human reviewer; PA-12.1 CI check (specified, **not implemented**); PA-12.3 retrospective note on the 31 historical lines — **not invalidated, history not rewritten**.
- SDP-001 v1.2 DRAFT: §3.3, §4.4 control 1, §7.1 (states `main` is not protected), §7.2, new §7.4 (who records an approval; review record per PR), §9.

## 2. PRB-001 — MSMask path counts the third ventricle as periventricular (HAZ-005 → HAZ-008)
`docs/iec62304/records/problem_reports/PRB-001_MSMask_Third_Ventricle_Counted_Periventricular.md` — first problem-report record (SPR-001 template; no GitHub Issue exists in this repository; the owner raises one).
- MSMask label 4 (lateral + third ventricle) is the PV landmark, against REQ-FUNC-053, IFU-001 §10.3 and Filippi 2019; LST-AI zones path inherits it. Paper D (PR #61), device's own functions: **3 of 3,992 expert lesions (0.08 %) change region; 0 of 124 DIS decisions change.**
- Severity **Minor, safety-related** (proposed). SPR-001 §4.1 requires a CAPA (Class C item): proposed as CAPA-006 action CA-6.14 (owner decision).
- Fix and verification proposed (lateral-only derived landmark, fail closed, `test_rc059_*`, regression on paper D's scans, negative controls). **`ms_region_classifier.py` (Class C) not touched.** RC-059 proposed, NOT IMPLEMENTED.

## 3. RMF-OBS-001 — the live longitudinal view presents several false new/enlarging lesions per patient (HAZ-007)
RMF-001 §3.5 (draft). Paper C pilot (PR #60) incl. arm A4 (expert change masks, 2026-10-22): the device's rule on FLAMeS masks proposed **≥ 1 false new/enlarging candidate in 20/20 patients [0.83–1.00], 8.9 per patient [5.8–12.6]; after its own subtraction "confirmation" 19/20, 5.4 per patient**; MSLesSeg 25/25, 8.2 per patient. No stable patients.
- Today (code read): review is **stated, not enforced**; counts shown under an "Active-disease CANDIDATE … MAGNIMS 2021: any new or enlarging T2 lesion marks activity" banner and a "NEDA-3 … activity CANDIDATE" badge; subtraction worded as "confirmed" / "supports a genuine new lesion"; safety texts English-only in all languages; no check of scanner/protocol change.
- Proposed: observation **Major, safety-related** (Critical before any clinical use); HAZ-007 probability P5; HAZ-007 "ACCEPTABLE" withdrawn → UNDETERMINED. Interim controls: **RC-060** never "activity" from unconfirmed candidates (target: per-candidate confirmation by the reader), **RC-061** measured false-candidate rate stated in the user's language and subtraction never worded as confirmation, **RC-062** abstain on acquisition change. REQ-SAFE-037 proposed. The calibrated subtraction threshold (A4: ~1.1 SD, 0.15 false/patient, 28 % of expert lesions kept) is **not** proposed as a control until validated on stable patients (secondary arm; failed on MSLesSeg).

## Other changes
- `capa_register.md`: CAPA-012 row; new section listing PRB-001 and RMF-OBS-001 with proposed CAPA links (CA-6.14, CA-8.11/12/13).
- TM-001 1.8: REQ-FUNC-053 / REQ-FUNC-054 annotated; addendum RC-059..RC-062 (NOT IMPLEMENTED, no test).
- `rc_test_manifest.json`: RC-059..RC-062 as `not_implemented`.

## Checks run
- Manifest JSON valid; `tests/unit/test_risk_control_manifest.py`: **336 passed**.
- Tests that read the controlled documents (CAPA-006/008/009, RC-010/025/029/032): 211 passed, 7 failed — all 7 in `test_rc032_region_atlas_guard.py` with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'skimage'` (local environment; no code changed by this PR).
- Added lines scanned: none records an approval.
- No cloud commands.

## Owner decisions needed
CAPA-012: D-1 severity, D-2 approval mechanism, D-3 retrospective confirmation of the 31 lines, D-4 independent reviewer, D-5 SDP-001 v1.2 text, D-6 CI check as a separate PR. PRB-001: severity and CAPA linkage. RMF-OBS-001: severity, HAZ-007 probability/determination, interim controls RC-060 (b)/RC-061/RC-062.

pull_requests.body:
**DRAFT — do not merge. Merge after #52, #51, #53, #59, #49 and #62.** Based on `qms/capa012-and-problem-reports` (PR #62). Nothing deployed; no cloud command was run.

Implements **REQ-SAFE-037** (a)–(e). Risk controls **RC-060, RC-061, RC-062** for **HAZ-007** (HAZ-003 for report drafts). Record: **CAPA-013** (draft). Every approval field: **PENDING owner approval**.

## Why

RMF-OBS-001 (PR #62), from the paper C pilot (PR #60): against **expert** change masks (open_ms, 20 patients, FLAMeS 5-fold), the device's new/enlarging rule proposed **≥ 1 false candidate in 20/20 patients, 8.9 per patient** (5.4 after its own subtraction check); MSLesSeg 25/25. Verified in the code of PR #62 before changing anything:

- the view showed these counts under **"Active-disease CANDIDATE"** / "Dissemination-in-time CANDIDATE" and a **"NEDA-3 MRI (T2-arm): activity CANDIDATE"** badge (`LongitudinalCompare.tsx:452-488`), from `activity_candidate` / `dit_candidate` returned by the route;
- review was stated in a caveat, never recorded;
- subtraction worded as "**confirmed** brighter at follow-up", "supports a genuine new lesion";
- **24 of 40** texts of the view had no es/de entry, 3 were hard-coded, dates `en-US`, and the backend's English caveat took precedence over the translated one;
- no scanner/protocol check between visits;
- consumers: the AI assistant received the raw flags; the `ms_longitudinal` report template asked for "**Active** / Not active" and NEDA-3; the report panel and the exports carry no longitudinal data (checked).

## What changed (minimal; segmentation, matching and the counting rule untouched)

| Control | Change |
|---|---|
| RC-060 (b) | `longitudinal_candidate_safety.present_comparison` is the single presentation step: legacy flags removed from every response; `change_candidates` (new ≥ 3 mm, enlarging, awaiting review, confirmed, rejected). View: "N unconfirmed change candidates … to be reviewed one by one by a radiologist"; no activity/DIT/NEDA text. Assistant client drops the flags at any depth. Report prompt: unconfirmed candidates as such; template without an Active/Not active class; a **fixed localised notice written by code** ends each draft that received a comparison |
| RC-060 (a), (c) | `POST /segmentation/longitudinal/review`: object authorization (RC-029), **radiologists only** (403, as RC-047), **bound to the SHA-256 of both masks** (409), reader + time stored on the follow-up segmentation; not on the assistant's compute-only list. `reader_confirmed_activity` exists only after ≥ 1 confirmation (MAGNIMS 2021 on confirmed candidates only) — the only place the word "activity" appears. Confirm / Reject per candidate in the table |
| RC-061 | Versioned asset `services/assets/longitudinal_false_candidate_evidence.json` v1.0.0 (paper C A4, source record path, commit `0501bd1`, SHA-256), **bound to the rule parameters** (3 mm, 20 %, IoU 0.3, 0.5 SD) — otherwise no rate and the view says so; no figure in a component. Subtraction = "a signal, not a confirmation". Every text of the view in **en/es/de**, no English default |
| RC-062 | Acquisition compared: manufacturer, model, field strength, 2D/3D, slice thickness (required); TR/TE/TI and slice spacing (when recorded); voxel size. Differs or not established → **abstain**: no candidates, counts, burden change or decisions; reason + metadata compared stated; overlay kept. PACS import now stores the acquisition record (DICOM header). **Consequence today: images uploaded as NIfTI have no record, so their comparisons abstain** (CAPA-013 D-3) |

**Identifiers.** PR #62 reserved RC-060/061/062 and REQ-SAFE-037 for exactly these controls; they are implemented under those IDs (not renumbered, to avoid two IDs per control). Next free IDs checked on every open branch: RC-063, REQ-SAFE-038, REQ-FUNC-100, CAPA-013 (used here). Docs: SRS 1.10, RMF 1.12, TM 1.9 (drafts), CAPA-013 record, register entry, manifest RC-060/061/062 → implemented (RC-035 note).

## Class C module modified

`backend/app/services/brain_report_service.py` — only the `ms_longitudinal` template and the longitudinal block of the prompt builder. Strictly necessary: the instruction to classify "Active / Not active" from interval counts lives in that template; nothing upstream can remove an instruction from the system prompt. RC-006 disclaimer and other templates unchanged. **Needs the Class C code review by a person other than the author (CAPA-013 D-5).** No other Class C module touched; `longitudinal_tracking_service.py` (the rule) unchanged.

## Verification

- **Tests written first, failing on PR #62:** `backend/tests/unit/test_capa013_longitudinal_candidates.py` (41 cases) and `frontend/src/components/LongitudinalCompare.capa013.test.tsx` (13 cases, drives the real panel). Re-run on the PR #62 sources by `scripts/safety/capa013_tests_on_base.py`: backend **40 of 41 fail**, frontend **13 of 13 fail**, with the reason of each recorded in `docs/iec62304/records/risk_verification/CAPA-013_tests_on_base_2026-10-22.json` (the one passing case is a regression guard).
- **After the fix:** 41/41 and 13/13. Whole backend tree (`pytest tests`): 1611 passed, 20 skipped, 5 xfailed, 1 failed — `test_auth_endpoints.py::TestWebAuthnEndpoints::test_webauthn_credentials_endpoint_exists` (`webauthn` not installed locally; fails identically on PR #62). Full frontend suite (`vitest --pool=threads`): 36 files, 283 tests — 280 passed, 3 skipped (FLAMeS tests needing local research data), 0 failed. `tsc --noEmit` clean; `vite build` passes. Existing tests adjusted: `test_rc029_*` / `test_capa009_*` (new route classified), `test_brain_report_service.py` (new labels).
- **Negative controls:** `scripts/safety/capa013_negative_controls.py` — **45 mutations, 45 detected** (RC-060: B1–B15, F1–F5; RC-061: E1–E6, F6–F12, F15; RC-062: A1–A9, F13–F14), record `CAPA-013_negative_controls_2026-10-22.json`. The first run left F12 (German rate text partly in English) undetected → the language test now refuses any English three-word phrase in es/de texts and in the rendered es/de panel, F15 added. A full-tree run then showed one new test using `asyncio.run` broke 100 later async tests (event loop cleared) → made a native async test; mutations re-executed against the final tests (per-mutation time and test hashes in the record).
- Not done: real-browser run, Firestore / real PACS import, usability (IEC 62366), radiologist review of es/de wording.

## Owner decisions (PENDING owner approval)

D-1 severity (Major, safety-related; Critical before clinical use) · D-2 CAPA-013 instead of CAPA-008 CA-8.11–8.13 · D-3 accept abstention for uploaded NIfTI until an acquisition capture path exists · D-4 es/de wording · D-5 Class C code review · D-6 merge order.

**DRAFT — one release branch for a single owner sign-off. Do not merge before the owner records his own approvals. Nothing deployed; no cloud command was run.** Every approval field still reads **PENDING owner approval** — none was changed or written here.

## What this branch is

`release/owner-signoff-2026-10` = `fix/longitudinal-activity-display-capa013` (PR #63, which already contains #52, #51, #53, #49 and #62) **+ a merge of PR #59** (`feat/slice-thickness-reliability`, history kept) **+ four fixes asked by the independent review of #59 and #62** (one commit each). Merging this PR merges all seven; the seven draft PRs can then be closed as merged here.

Chain (oldest first): #52 CAPA-010 → #51 CAPA-011 → #53 in-browser FLAMeS (flag OFF) → #49 SDP-001 v1.1 → #62 CAPA-012 / PRB-001 / RMF-OBS-001 → #63 CAPA-013 → **#59 slice-thickness card (flag OFF)** → review fixes.

### Conflicts resolved in the #59 merge (`a074456`; documents only; both sides kept, in the order #59 reserved)

| Document | Result |
|---|---|
| SRS-001 | revisions 1.5 (#52), 1.6 (#51), 1.7 (#53), **1.8 (#59)**, 1.9 (#62), 1.10 (#63); REQ-SAFE-025..033, **034..036 (#59)**, 037; REQ-FUNC-098/099 (#59) in §2.5. Header: 1.10 |

| `rc_test_manifest.json` | auto-merged; RC-054..058 moved between RC-053 and RC-059 (content unchanged). Valid JSON, 61 controls, **every listed test exists** (76 entries) |

- No duplicated identifier: REQ-SAFE-001..037, REQ-FUNC up to 099, HAZ-001..015, RC-001..062 each defined once (RC-010 twice by design: the superseded 2026-07-18 row is kept as history).
- The three #59 version-header lines ("1.8 / 1.10 / 1.7 DRAFT … merge after #52, #51 and #53") are replaced by the chain's later header lines, which already list #59 (the same happened to #53's header lines in the earlier merge).

### Fixes asked by the independent review of #59 and #62 (one commit each)

| # | Commit | Finding | Fix | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (#59) | `d45a98e` | An ORIGINAL 2D DICOM **without SliceThickness but with SpacingBetweenSlices 2.5 mm** was reported as "2.5 mm, from the header" — the spacing is not the thickness (REQ-SAFE-034 (c)) | `acquisition_geometry.py`: without a valid SliceThickness the result is **not determinable** (reason `missing`/`invalid`), whatever the spacing | Tests first: `test_rc054_spacing_without_thickness_is_not_determinable` (4 cases) and `test_rc054_loader_never_reports_the_spacing_as_the_thickness` (real loader) **failed before** (`('native', 2.5)`), pass after; new negative control **B13** |
| 2 (#59) | `06680cc` | Between 1.5 and 3.5 mm the card used rows added **after** paper A's results were seen ("8 of 10 from 50 mm³" at 2 mm), while the pre-registered band 1.5–4.5 mm gives **no size** | Evidence asset **v2.0.0** (`sliceThicknessReliability.v2.json`): only the protocol's pre-registered bands (≤ 1.5 as delivered, 1.5–4.5, 4.5–6.5, > 6.5 mm), each fed only by its own row; the three post-hoc MSLesSeg rows removed (named under `excluded_post_hoc`, kept in the research record only); `validateAsset` refuses a post-hoc row or record; post-hoc marker removed from the card. SRS REQ-SAFE-036, RMF RC-056/RC-057, TM rows, manifest updated | Tests first: on the v1 asset **10 of 41 failed** (incl. "a natively 2 mm study is not told 8 in 10 from 50 mm³"); now pass. Negative controls **D5 redefined, D10, D11 added** |
| 3 (#62) | `8c0c39d` | Severities below the project's procedures: QP-002 §5 classes regulatory non-compliance (and patient safety risk) as Critical; SPR-001 §2 classes any safety impact as Critical | **CAPA-012 Major → Critical**; **PRB-001 Minor → Critical**; **RMF-OBS-001 Major → Critical** — in each record, RMF-001 §3.5/§7.2, revision note and CAPA register; due dates of CAPA-012 recomputed on the Critical timeline (+7 d / +30 d) like every other Critical CAPA. **CAPA-013 states its severity "as RMF-OBS-001" and was raised with it** (one step beyond the review's list — owner decides, D-1) | Documents only; all severities remain *proposed* |
| 4 (#62) | `041836b` | PRB-001 said a lesion touching only the third ventricle "is classified periventricular" | Stated exactly: in paper D **3 of the 6** such expert lesions were classified periventricular (G0), 4 of 4 with the LST-AI registration (G1); same wording in RMF §3.5 cause (f) and revision note | Paper D `RESULTS.md` §7 (record `S4_ventricles`) |

## Per PR: what changes for clinicians, and the review evidence

| PR | What changes for a clinician | Review evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **#52** CAPA-010 (viewer) | Patient name/MRN now shown in the 3D view and in every multi-panel cell; no L/R letters or orientation cube in 3D; the selected lesion's 3D crosshair/box at the right voxel (was transposed); ruler, area and angle correct at any zoom/pan and in mm; the "laterality not labelled" caveat visible at common screen sizes | **Adversarial review done** (PR #52 review: commits `db4f1af`, `8b839fd`); tests first on `main` (25 of 27 fail for the stated reason); real-browser before/after probe; negative controls |
| **#51** CAPA-011 (clinical-tool masks) | Masks from FLAMeS / LST-AI / SynthSeg / mindGlide load at the voxel where the tool put them (were transposed twice); a mask that cannot be placed, or is not on the image's grid, is not stored and the run fails with a stated reason. Tools are off in production, so nothing visible today | **Adversarial pre-merge review done** (`86f19f2`, grid check); 14 round-trip tests fail on `main`; negative controls |
| **#53** in-browser FLAMeS (flag `VITE_ENABLE_BROWSER_FLAMES` **OFF**) | Nothing while the flag is OFF (proved below). The server side is live but only concerns AI drafts: AI provenance stored, an AI draft stays "unreviewed" until a radiologist confirms the exact stored mask, any later mask change resets the review | **Two adversarial reviews done** (first review + re-review 2, `docs/research/flames-in-browser/REVIEW-RESPONSE.md`); the reviewed code fails the new tests 6/6; negative controls |
| **#49** SDP-001 v1.1 | Nothing (documentation: the AI coding agent declared as a development tool) | Documentation only |
| **#62** CAPA-012, PRB-001, RMF-OBS-001 | Nothing (documentation only: approval/review-record process, third-ventricle problem report, longitudinal over-call observation; RC-059 proposed, not implemented) | **No independent review when the PR was written.** An independent review of the release branch (2026-10-23) asked for fixes 3 and 4 above, applied here |
| **#63** CAPA-013 (longitudinal) | The comparison no longer shows "Active-disease CANDIDATE", "Dissemination-in-time CANDIDATE" or a NEDA badge: it shows "N unconfirmed change candidates", each confirmable/rejectable by a radiologist (recorded, bound to both masks); the measured false-candidate rate is stated in en/es/de; FLAIR subtraction is "a signal, not a confirmation"; when scanner/protocol differ or cannot be established (today: **every comparison of images uploaded as NIfTI**) the view abstains — no counts, reason stated, overlay kept; report drafts never state a reader decision and end with a fixed notice. Changes the Class C `brain_report_service.py` (template + prompt block) | **Adversarial review done** (comment on PR #63: 2 blockers + 6 findings fixed, tests first `be9ae55`, fixes `a1c41e2`); tests first on PR #62 (40/41 + 13/13 fail); negative controls. **Class C code review by a person other than the author still required (CAPA-013 D-5)** |
| **#59** slice-thickness card (flag `VITE_ENABLE_SLICE_THICKNESS_RELIABILITY` **OFF**) | Nothing visible while the flag is OFF (proved below). Backend: every loaded image now carries `metadata.acquisition_geometry` (native / at least / not determinable); nothing displays it with the flag OFF | **No independent review when the PR was written.** An independent review of the release branch (2026-10-23) asked for fixes 1 and 2 above, applied here with tests first and new negative controls |

## Verification on this branch (after the review fixes, `041836b`; the last commit `e870e89` only adds the negative-control record)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Frontend suite `npx vitest run --pool=threads` | **36 files passed, 3 skipped; 331 tests passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed** (skipped = opt-in FLAMeS harnesses needing local research data: parity, gate validation, gate replay). Includes the CAPA-010 real-browser layout check |
| Type check `npx tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| Production build `npx vite build` (`.env.production`, no flag set) | built. Bundled env object `{BASE_URL:"/",DEV:!1,MODE:"production",PROD:!0,SSR:!1,VITE_API_BASE_URL:"https://brain-mri-7bp6oqdu7a-uc.a.run.app"}` — neither `VITE_ENABLE_BROWSER_FLAMES` nor `VITE_ENABLE_SLICE_THICKNESS_RELIABILITY` is present; the flags compile to `BROWSER_FLAMES:Zt("ENABLE_BROWSER_FLAMES",!1)` and `SLICE_THICKNESS_RELIABILITY:Zt("ENABLE_SLICE_THICKNESS_RELIABILITY",!1)` → both **false**. Render gates: `fn.BROWSER_FLAMES&&…Suspense…` and `fn.SLICE_THICKNESS_RELIABILITY&&…Suspense…`, both lazy chunks. The FLAMeS model URL (`/models/flames/flames-fold0-2a10bb9d.onnx`) occurs **only** in `BrowserFlamesCard-*.js`; the FLAMeS worker is referenced only from that chunk; **no `.onnx` file and no `models/` folder in `dist/`**; `index.html` preloads only the vendor chunks → **the model is never requested while the flag is OFF**. The card, its logic and the v2 evidence asset (`2.0.0`, no `MSL_` row) occur only in `SliceThicknessReliabilityCard-*.js`. (The `ort-wasm` files in `dist/` belong to the existing Edge-AI screening worker.) Licences present: Apache-2.0, flames-NOTICE, onnxruntime-web-MIT |
| Backend unit suite (`pytest tests/unit`) | **1508 passed, 0 failed** (incl. `test_rc054_*` 39, `test_capa013_*`, `test_rc039_*`, `test_rc047_*`, risk-control manifest gate) |
| Backend integration (CI filter) | 25 passed, 1 failed — `test_webauthn_credentials_endpoint_exists`: `webauthn` is not installed in the local environment (local only; same on #51, #62, #63) |

## CAPA-015 — durable audit trail and session continuation (DRAFT — PENDING owner approval)

**Merge after CAPA-014** (parallel PR holding RC-064..066, REQ-SEC-021..023, SRS 1.11, RMF 1.13, TM 1.10). **Do not merge, do not deploy.** No cloud command run; every backend test run under PRB-002 isolation (missing credentials file, empty gcloud configuration, project `mstool-offline-tests`). Once PR #66 (permanent test guard) is merged, this branch will be rebased onto it, keeping its in-memory audit and refresh-store lines.

Implements **REQ-SEC-024, REQ-SEC-025, REQ-SEC-026** (SRS 1.12). Risk controls **RC-067, RC-068, RC-069** for **HAZ-010** (and **HAZ-001** for unsaved segmentation work) — RMF 1.14, TM 1.11. Record: `docs/iec62304/records/capa/CAPA-015_Audit_Trail_And_Session_Continuation.md` (§10 = independent review, §11 = re-review).

### What was wrong (confirmed in `main` @ 70cc5c7)
1. **Audit trail not durable**: `logs/audit.log` on the instance disk; `/auth/audit-logs` read an in-memory list; Firestore `audit_logs` never written. Login, segmentation save/confirm, AI report generation, longitudinal decisions were never audited; query strings (`?token=`) copied into records; trail readable by radiologists.
2. **No session refresh**: `/auth/refresh` did not exist; one 60-minute token; unsaved segmentation lost or unsaveable at expiry; hard redirect on 401.
3. Found while verifying: password change not effective at sign-in; logout revocation in an unused token manager; tests reached the real Firestore with developer credentials (PRB-002, permanent guard in PR #66).

### What changes
- **RC-067**: stdout JSON + append-only Firestore `audit_logs` (`create()`, server time); one record per API request (actor, role, route template, resource ids, outcome, request id); clinical routes mapped; every other `/auth` request recorded (passkey registration start as its own event, register/delete, user reads, 5xx); reads deduplicated; **only anonymous records budgeted per source — every authenticated record durable**; keyed HMAC identifiers; coarse user agent; **client address chosen by no client-sent header** (right-most `X-Forwarded-For` entry, stepping left only over the published Firebase Hosting / Fastly egress list, replaceable by `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`); never blocks; admin-only paginated reader, status and banner.
- **RC-068**: 15-min access token; rotating refresh token in `__session` (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, `/api/v1/auth`, app origin via Firebase Hosting rewrite); SHA-256 stored; rotation in one transaction; 30-s grace window, real reuse revokes the family; 30 min idle / 12 h absolute; start-up refuses idle ≤ access + 2 min; revoked on logout / password change / inactive or locked account; store error → 503 without revocation; password change persisted. Logout revokes the access token **per server instance** only (documented).
- **RC-069**: silent renewal before the earlier deadline; one refresh shared by requests and tabs (15-s limit); 401/403/404/405 → same-user re-login dialog, work kept, waiting requests retried; several tabs handled; **a tab only ever sends its own user's token**; **the page behind the dialog stays mounted but is hidden, inert and blurred**.

### Re-review of `09e11e8` — corrected (CAPA-015 §11)
- **N1** client IP: no longer depends on `X-Forwarded-Host` (client-sent); egress list embedded with source URL and date, update procedure in `core/client_ip.py`. **N1b**: the list now matches https://api.fastly.com/public-ip-list as fetched on 2026-10-24 by the coordinating agent (24 ranges; the first transcription lacked `90.98.0.0/17`, `90.98.128.0/18`, `2a04:4e44::/32` and had `2a04:4e42::/32` instead of `/31`), pinned by a test.
- **N4** budget: anonymous records only; Cloud Logging keeps **7 days** in this project (CAPA §4, §7, D-3 corrected); REQ-SEC-024 reworded.
- **N3** `getAccessToken()` in ImageViewer3D and ProfilePage; `fetchWithSession` drops a caller's `Authorization`; source scan test.
- **N2** `tests/conftest.py` sets the three lifetimes; checklist line for developers' `.env`.
- **N5** page hidden/inert/blurred behind the re-login dialog (owner may relax, D-5).
- Nits: `register/begin` → `auth.credential.register_begin`; RMF RC-068 per-instance logout; CAPA sections re-ordered.

### Verification (author — not independent)
- Tests first: on `main` 70cc5c7 backend 29/29 and frontend 12/12 fail; review cases on `2c618ec` backend 18/47 and frontend 9/9 fail; re-review cases on `09e11e8` **backend 8/25 and frontend 3/3 fail** (records in `docs/iec62304/records/risk_verification/`).
- After: CAPA-015 tests backend 55/55, frontend 24/24. Backend tree **1772 passed, 20 skipped, 5 xfailed, 1 failed** (`test_webauthn_credentials_endpoint_exists` — `webauthn` not installed locally; same on `main`). Frontend **355 passed, 3 skipped**; type check clean; production build passes.

- Not verified: real Firestore, real browser (`inert` and blur checked in jsdom only), deployed Hosting rewrite/cookie, Hosting's real egress address (the list was fetched once by the coordinating agent; refresh it before go-live), Cloud Run CPU throttling.

### Owner actions
- **Before go-live:** refresh the egress list from https://api.fastly.com/public-ip-list and confirm the recorded client address through a **Firebase Hosting preview channel** (`DEPLOYMENT_CHECKLIST.md` step 1b). A wrong list is fixed with a Cloud Run settings update (`TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`), without a rebuild.
- **`CLAUDE.md`**: `test_endpoints.sh` now has 10 checks ([0] `--hosting-only` and [9] added); `CLAUDE.md` still says "all 9 checks must PASS" — not edited by this PR, owner to update.
- Deployment per `DEPLOYMENT_CHECKLIST.md`: lifetimes check; backend, preview-channel check, then hosting, outside clinical hours; users reload; indexes only (rules: diff first, D-8).

### Owner decisions (all PENDING)
D-1 severity Critical · D-2 lifetimes 15 min / 30 min / 12 h · D-3 audit retention (6 years Firestore; Cloud Logging 7 days or a 400-day bucket) · D-4 Hosting rewrite · D-5 inactivity log-off / blur behind the dialog · D-6 radiologists' `AUDIT_VIEW` · D-7 alerting · D-8 Firestore rules · D-9 `AUDIT_HASH_KEY` · D-10 grace window 30 s. pull_requests.title: PRB-002: backend tests can never reach a real Google Cloud service (DRAFT)
pull_requests.head: fix/test-cloud-isolation-prb002
pull_requests.body:
## What changed and why

**Problem report PRB-002** (`docs/iec62304/records/problem_reports/PRB-002_Local_Test_Runs_Wrote_To_Production_User_Store.md`).

On a developer computer with gcloud application-default credentials, local backend test runs used the **production** Firestore (`brain-mri-476110`): they listed the encrypted `auth_users` collection and wrote test accounts into it. Surviving local logs show 112 writes and 62 test accounts between 2026-07-12 and 2026-10-24. Each account has a new random id, so nothing existing was overwritten. The accounts are encrypted with the public test key, so production cannot decrypt them and they cannot be used to log in. No patient or clinical data was involved, and no data of any other project was read or written. CI has no credentials, which is why CI never showed the problem.

`backend/tests/conftest.py` now sets five independent layers before any application import. A test catches an app module imported earlier.

1. `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` is **forced** to a missing file, and `GCS_CREDENTIALS_FILE` is emptied.
2. `CLOUDSDK_CONFIG` points at an empty, git-ignored folder.
3. `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` is set to `mstool-offline-tests`. Keys and endpoints of other external services are removed (Anthropic, tool endpoints, Vertex, Redis, PACS).
4. `google.auth.default` **always** raises, also with the `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST` that CI sets without an emulator.
5. Python sockets, and on Windows asyncio's default proactor, may only connect to loopback; HTTP proxies are switched off.

## Independent review

The first version (1bd6d69) was reviewed adversarially before merge. Main finding: CI's emulator variable made that version hand anonymous credentials to every Google client, and fallback routes hung for minutes in a CI simulation. All findings were addressed in 5396d4b and 7054932. A re-review of 8bd7fe4 closed them and found five minor points (N1 to N5; main one: on Windows, asyncio's proactor bypassed the socket guard), addressed in 2cb0f73. See section 6 of the PRB-002 record.

## Traceability

- Problem report **PRB-002**. Proposed severity **Critical**, the conservative reading of "data corruption" in the SPR-001 section 2 table; the owner decides between Critical and Major. Not safety-related; no Class C module is touched.
- Test configuration only; no application module changed.

## Verification

- `backend/tests/unit/test_prb002_no_cloud_in_tests.py`: 19 tests. They cover the guard being installed before any app import, each layer, the start-up user-store singleton and `AuthService`, CI's emulator variable, and outbound connections refused while loopback is allowed.
- Negative controls `scripts/safety/prb002_negative_controls.py`: **19/19 detected**. M9 re-creates the first version's emulator branch; M10 imports the app before the guard.
- The base without the guard was deliberately **not** run "failing first": on this computer it writes to production.
- Full backend suite locally: 1715 passed, 20 skipped, 5 xfailed. One test fails because the local venv lacks the `webauthn` package (it is in requirements.txt; CI installs it).
- Integration step run the CI way (emulator variable set, same `-k` filter): 25 passed, the same 1 webauthn failure, 6 s, no hang.

## Owner decisions pending

- (a) Remove the 62 test records from production `auth_users`. The ids are kept locally, not in this public repo.
- (b) Follow-up: outside Cloud Run the backend should not default to the production project. Production already sets `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`.
- Approve the PRB-002 record and its severity.

Merge before #65. CAPA-015 then rebases onto this conftest and keeps its memory backends.

pull_requests.head: fix/ai-report-deidentification-capa014
pull_requests.body:
## CAPA-014 — AI report draft: no free text leaves the application (DRAFT, redesigned, reviewed three times, final and last checks)

**Do not merge.** Draft for owner review. Nothing has been deployed and no cloud command was run. All approval fields read "PENDING owner approval".

### What changed and why

**Defect (verified on `main` @ `70cc5c7` with tests written first).** `POST /api/v1/ai/report/generate` forwarded everything to Anthropic (`claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`) verbatim:
- the clinician's free text;
- the exact age;
- every string of the findings;
- any value placed in fields printed without a number format.

Meanwhile the Class C service header, the API client and the footer of every draft claimed de-identification and HIPAA compliance. This is the same gap as RC-007′ (2026-07-18) and CAPA-001 CA-4.

**First version (`4bfdd7e`), rejected by an independent adversarial review.** It scrubbed free text with regular expressions. The review found that it:
- still leaked the patient's own identifiers: 9-digit phones, "9. 11. 1975", "9-Nov-1975", "geb. 9.11.", particle surnames, soft hyphens and zero-width characters, names written together, "Muenchen";
- had a residual check that shared those rules, so it could not see the leaks;
- rewrote the device's labels: "Deep [name removed] Matter" for a patient named White;
- left ages of 90 and over exact;
- ran in quadratic time (27 s on 80 KB);
- left more false claims in place than the CAPA admitted.

**Redesign (ISO 14971 §7.1, inherent safety by design first), completed after the second review:**
- **RC-064, structured payload only** (`report_payload_guard.provider_payload`, new; part of the Class C report item):
  - Measurements are sent as numbers. A value that is not a number is sent as "not available", never as 0. A number outside the physical range of its field (a date, a record number or a phone number in a number field) refuses the request: 503, nothing sent. Exceptions: a burden change without a physical bound is "not available", a confidence outside 0–1 is left out, voxel counts go up to 2^31, and a rounding error at an edge is accepted. A whole number equal to the patient's own record number, phone number or birth date (as digits, checked against the patient record) refuses the request in any number field.
  - Labels come only from the device's fixed vocabulary, which now holds every label name the application ships. Any other label becomes "[unlisted label N]", one number per label in groups and rows; the draft tells the clinician which label each number stands for (never sent).
  - Sex is sent only as M or F, and age as a 5-year band ("90 or older" from 90).
  - A DIS result keeps its evaluation state. A DIS that is not evaluated or has no conclusion is sent as "not evaluated", never as "NOT MET" (coordination with PR #68, below).
  - No free-text field and no unknown field is sent; only a flag that the clinician typed something.
  - The prompt builder (Class C `brain_report_service.py`) prints no free text, even when called directly.
- **RC-065, fail closed plus a detection-only tripwire:**
  - The analysed segmentation is required (400, not 422, because the panel reads every 422 as "no measurements") and must be authorized for the caller (`authorize_segmentation_id`, 404).
  - The patient record must be readable and complete (503).
  - The tripwire checks the final prompt after NFKC, removal of format characters (soft hyphen, zero-width characters, BOM) and look-alike/accent mapping. On any finding nothing is sent (503). It looks for:
    - the patient's own identifiers from the record: name, also written together, with German spellings, or as a pair; record number (letters and digits with up to 3 separators; all-digit numbers and the digits of a prefixed one as a whole number, not inside a decimal number or before a unit); birth date in numeric, month-name, Roman and partial forms; phone with and without country code and trunk 0; e-mail; contact; city; street;
    - generic patterns: e-mail, dated text, "+" phones, long or grouped numbers, ID-like tokens, titled names.
  - It never edits text. It never reports the device's own words alone (only words the user prompt can contain, not the system templates), nor two of them in the order the device's text has them ("Deep White").
  - It is capped at 400 000 characters and uses only linear patterns.
- **RC-066, the draft, true statements and records:**
  - **The clinician's typed text is added to the draft by the route after the model returns**, right after the RC-006 disclaimer, under "Clinician's entry (added in the application; not sent to the AI service)". It is shown exactly as typed in a quoted block (nothing in it is rendered as a heading, image, link or HTML) and closed by a rule. The model's text always follows under the fixed heading "AI draft (from measurements only)". The model is told about the entry only when something was typed. The report viewer never loads an image named in a draft. The entry and the application's notes are **separate response fields** (`clinician_entry`, `app_notes`, next to `disclaimer`, `ai_draft_heading`, `ai_text`). The viewer and its print view render them in boxes of their own, outside the Markdown renderer, so nothing the model writes can produce them; any fenced block in the AI text is an ordinary code block. `content` stays the whole draft as one text for copy, export and the assistant, assembled from the fields with the fixed headings and plain quoting. The model's text loses every Unicode format character, and a line that is exactly one of the application's headings is replaced; ordinary sentences stay as written. Bidirectional control characters are removed from the typed text. Each typed field holds at most 5000 characters (the panel shows a counter; a longer text from another caller is cut with a visible "[truncated …]" line).
  - The log records counts of what was withheld, never the payload.
  - The panel note and the report viewer footer (en/es/de) now say that only the measurements, sex and a 5-year age range are sent. The old `hipaaNote` key is removed.
  - False claims are corrected in README (badge removed), TD-001, AIA-001, ISMS-001, CSA-001, DD-001, the master document, the technical documentation (also its model name) and its PDF generator; the audit-record generator no longer writes the withdrawn RC-007 statement.
  - A repository-wide test fails on any new claim; historical records are allow-listed.
- The scrubbing module of the first version and its tests are removed.

**UI:** the panel note and the report viewer footer change. In the draft, the typed text appears under its own heading in a quoted block, and the model's text under "AI draft (from measurements only)". A measurement that is missing prints "not available". The entry and the note on unlisted labels have their own boxes; each typed field shows a counter and stops at 5000 characters.

### Second independent review (N1–N10) and how each was fixed (details: CAPA-014 §8.1)

The re-review closed the 8 findings of the first review (0 of 77 planted markers reached the provider, no false refusal for the collision names, linear time) and raised 10 more:

| # | Finding | Fix | Tests / mutations |
|---|---|---|---|
| N1 (major, HAZ-003) | Typed Markdown became report structure; the model's text could sit under the clinician's heading | Typed text quoted in a fenced block longer than any backtick run in it; entry closed; model text always under "AI draft (from measurements only)" | `test_n1_*` (en/es/de); M4–M7 |
| N2 | The app's own labels sent as "[unlisted label]"; "(n)" counted every label; rows and groups did not match; renamed labels invisible | Every shipped label name in the vocabulary (test reads every preset); "[unlisted label N]" once per label; named in the draft only | `test_n2_*`; P10–P12 |
| N3 | A non-number printed as 0 | "not available" | `test_n3_*`; P13 |
| N4 | No plausibility limits (20250042 as a centroid, 20240304 as a count) | Physical range per printed number; outside it: 503, nothing sent | `test_n4_*`; P14 |
| N5 | 421 exempt words from the system templates ("filippi", "will", "pons") | Exempt words only from what the user prompt can contain (221) | `test_n5_*`; T23 |
| N6 | Instruction about the clinician's entry sent even with nothing typed | Only when something was typed | `test_n6_*`; M8 |
| N7 | Typed image links rendered as external images (screen, print) | Quoted (N1); the viewer also never loads an image named in a draft | UI-CAPA014; U8 |
| N8 | 6–7-digit record numbers refused legitimate drafts ("12345.67 mm³", "123456 voxels") | Whole-number match, not inside a decimal number nor before a unit; the digits of a prefixed record number now checked. Remains: a whole number equal to it refuses (fail closed) | `test_n8_*`; T24, T25 |
| N9 | Generator could write the withdrawn RC-007 "strips PHI" text; stale "claude-3-5-sonnet" | Generator fixed and "strips PHI" added to the claims test; model name corrected | claims test, `test_n9_*`; C3, C4 |
| N10 | No dispositions in §8; REQ-SEC-022(d) said "any separators" | §8.1 table; REQ-SEC-022(d) states what the code does | SRS 1.11 |
| also | Patients named "Deep White", "Left Cerebral", "Juxta Cortical" refused on every draft | Pairs and joined words of the device's own text are not a name | collision tests; T26, T27 |

**Known limits of the tripwire** (they matter only if a text path reopens; CAPA-014 §8 item 2): a street name with a hyphen ("Leopold-Straße 12"), a city's name in another language ("Munich"), "Ms" before a surname ("Ms Do"), initials, the year of birth alone, names made only of device words in the device's order, all-digit record numbers under 6 digits.

### Third independent review (R1–R4, M1, M2) (details: CAPA-014 §8.2)

The third review found the branch ready for the owner's Class C review: 0 of 80 markers reached the provider, there were 0 false refusals, and all 14 hostile inputs stayed inside their block. Its minor items:

| # | Item | Fix | Tests / mutations |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The model could imitate the clinician's box (a "### Clinician's entry" heading plus a fenced block under the AI heading); bidirectional control characters | The entry and the app note are `clinician-entry` / `app-note` blocks shown in boxes of their own. The model's text loses any such block (made plain), any line that is one of the app's headings (replaced by a fixed line) and all bidi controls; typed text loses bidi controls too | `test_r1_*`, UI box case; M9–M13, U9 |
